# Agent Coordination

```txt
Document type: Area Portal
Audience: Human reviewer, maintainer and implementation agent
Purpose: Route current execution to its owners and retain historical evidence
Design status: Accepted
Implementation: Current-owner navigation; former coordination engine retired
Provenance: Owner A16 whole-area reframe; complete classified input retained in history/retired-engine/files
Writer type: Human + agent coauthor
Canonical for: Area navigation, not runtime schema or old engine status
Use this when: Locating current execution owners or historical coordination claims
Do not use this for: Reinstating the retired CoordinationSession engine
Last reviewed: Pending independent whole-area review
Related:
- docs/specs/runner.md
- docs/platform/agent-coordination/spec.md
- docs/platform/agent-coordination/history/retired-engine/README.md
Supersedes: Stale current-state framing only; no old claim is dropped
Superseded by: None
Added in candidate: Current-owner routing and retirement framing
```

## Current Execution

The former coordination engine was retired in `2180b4e72701bb090288af8fe8021008d9d42079`. `coordination` is not a current public CLI verb; the actual machine-readable `--help --json` manifest is the CLI inventory.

CollaborationPattern owns Unit collaboration patterns in `src/runner/execution/patterns/index.mjs`; Unit execution enters through `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`. Workflow execution belongs to `src/workflow/runner.mjs` and its Unit execution-core integration.
The surviving Assignment/Run dispatch chain is also current: Assignment building, DispatchPlan compilation, governed execution and RunResult normalization are owned by `src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs`, `plan.mjs`, `assignment-runner.mjs` and `run-result.mjs`.

Read [the runner spec](../../specs/runner.md) for the current execution contract, then [this area's current-owner map](spec.md). Do not treat CoordinationSession, CoordinationProtocol or FlowDefinition in the preserved documents as current implemented engine entities.

## Preserved History

The [complete previous portal](history/retired-engine/README.md#literal-snapshot) and [previous spec](history/retired-engine/spec.md#literal-snapshot) remain verbatim, including all original qualifications and statuses. They are non-authority history, not present implementation claims.

Use the snapshots to audit preserved claims. They do not reinstate the retired engine or strengthen proposal/implementation status.

- [Historical architecture](history/retired-engine/architecture/system-context.md#literal-snapshot)
- [Historical CLI proposal](history/retired-engine/proposals/semantic-cli-surface.md#literal-snapshot)
- [Historical implementation alignment](history/retired-engine/verification/implementation-alignment.md#literal-snapshot)
- [Retired documentation policies and migration plans](history/documentation-migration/documentation-governance.md)

## Surviving Current Material

The retired engine no longer defines this area's live runtime. Current material
is narrower, but not empty: it retains the dispatch/result/recovery boundaries
that have surviving executable owners, and four cognitive companions consumed
by the registered architecture-advisory skill. No current CoordinationSession,
FlowDefinition, CoordinationProtocol or `fgos coordination` contract is retained.

| Reading need | Current candidate material |
|---|---|
| Execution and Workflow ownership | [spec.md](spec.md), with links to the runner spec and executable owners |
| Retained dispatch boundary | [Dispatch control plane](architecture/dispatch-control-plane.md), [runtime model](architecture/runtime-model.md) |
| Evidence and outcome | [Evidence/results](architecture/evidence-and-results.md), [RunResult contract](contracts/assignment-run-runresult.md), [visibility](architecture/visibility-and-herdr.md) |
| Recovery and control | [Recovery](architecture/runtime-recovery-design.md), [run control](architecture/run-handle.md), [recovery choice](architecture/executor-health-and-fallback.md) |
| Work and result authority boundaries | [Work integration](architecture/work-integration.md), [ADR-001](decisions/ADR-001-work-lifecycle-authority.md), [ADR-003](decisions/ADR-003-assignment-run-runresult-separation.md), [ADR-005](decisions/ADR-005-herdr-visibility-only.md), [ADR-011](decisions/ADR-011-dispatch-owns-lifecycle-receiver-writes-receipt.md) |
| Cognitive advisory quality, not runtime recipes | [Coordinator companion](playbooks/prompts/architecture-advisory-coordinator.md), [role doctrine](playbooks/architecture-advisory-role-doctrine.md), [artifact templates](playbooks/architecture-advisory-artifact-templates.md), [evaluation rubric](playbooks/architecture-advisory-evaluation-rubric.md) |
| Dated physical evidence | [Verification index](verification/README.md); evidence payload bytes and paths remain unchanged |
| Legal Workflow operations and current vocabulary | [Operation contract](contracts/workflow-stage-operation.md), [vocabulary index](vocabulary/README.md), [trigger surface](architecture/group-thinking-trigger-surface.md) |
| Provenance, compatibility and domain harness decisions | [Decision index](decisions/README.md), including current ADR-002, ADR-004, ADR-006 and ADR-007 |

## Current Execution

The former coordination engine was retired in `2180b4e72701bb090288af8fe8021008d9d42079`. `coordination` is not a current public CLI verb; the actual machine-readable `--help --json` manifest is the CLI inventory.

CollaborationPattern owns Unit collaboration patterns in `src/runner/execution/patterns/index.mjs`; Unit execution enters through `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`. Workflow execution belongs to `src/workflow/runner.mjs` and its Unit execution-core integration.
The surviving Assignment/Run dispatch chain is also current: Assignment building, DispatchPlan compilation, governed execution and RunResult normalization are owned by `src/runner/dispatch/assignment.mjs`, `plan.mjs`, `assignment-runner.mjs` and `run-result.mjs`.

Read [the runner spec](../../specs/runner.md) for the current execution contract, then [this area's current-owner map](spec.md). Do not treat CoordinationSession, CoordinationProtocol or FlowDefinition in the preserved documents as current implemented engine entities.

> **Ghi chú (2026-10-14, decision 0062 trong `docs/specs/runner.md`):** các cửa dispatch thô mà tài liệu, proof và roadmap trong thư mục này nhắc tới — `dispatch execute` (cả `--contract`, `--assignment`), `dispatch log`, `dispatch fanout-batch` — đã bị xoá. Việc chạy qua `fgos run "<prompt>"` / `fgos run --unit` hoặc `fgos workflow start`. Các bản ghi verification/proof giữ nguyên lệnh đã chạy lúc đó, như bằng chứng lịch sử.

## Preserved History

The [complete previous portal](history/retired-engine/README.md#literal-snapshot) and [previous spec](history/retired-engine/spec.md#literal-snapshot) remain verbatim, including all original qualifications and statuses. They are non-authority history, not present implementation claims.

Use the snapshots to audit preserved claims. They do not reinstate the retired engine or strengthen proposal/implementation status.

- [Historical architecture](history/retired-engine/architecture/system-context.md#literal-snapshot)
- [Historical CLI proposal](history/retired-engine/proposals/semantic-cli-surface.md#literal-snapshot)
- [Historical implementation alignment](history/retired-engine/verification/implementation-alignment.md#literal-snapshot)
- [Retired documentation policies and migration plans](history/documentation-migration/documentation-governance.md)

## Surviving Current Material

The retired engine no longer defines this area's live runtime. Current material
is narrower, but not empty: it retains the dispatch/result/recovery boundaries
that have surviving executable owners, and four cognitive companions consumed
by the registered architecture-advisory skill. No current CoordinationSession,
FlowDefinition, CoordinationProtocol or `fgos coordination` contract is retained.

A caller in that layer may derive a capability or an\nexplicit executor-id from them before entering this control plane; none of\nthem becomes a third resolvable identity inside dispatch core. See\nComponent-Outer Boundary Note below.\n\n## Contracts\n\nThese three contracts are canonical for this control plane. They are\nadditive over the current implementation, not a replacement of it — see the\nImplementation Status line under each for what is real today versus still\nSlice D/E scope in the normalization plan.\n\n### DispatchRequest (outer → core)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"target\": { \"kind\": \"capability | executor\", \"value\": \"code:implement\" },\n  \"policy\": {\n    \"minTier\": \"standard\",\n    \"preferExecutor\": \"agy-herdr\",\n    \"fallbackExecutors\": [\"codex-herdr\"],\n    \"preferPersona\": \"code-reviewer\",\n    \"visibility\": \"headless\"\n  },\n  \"provenance\": {\n    \"source\": \"workflow-operation\",\n    \"domain\": \"coding\",\n    \"workflow\": \"feature\",\n    \"stage\": \"executing\",\n    \"operation\": \"implement-item\",\n    \"taskSpec\": \"implement-item\",\n    \"skill\": \"fgos-coding-implement\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- `target.kind: capability` resolves through `runner.capabilities` and\n  executor `for[]` bindings.\n- `target.kind: executor` is an explicit concrete override and remains\n  visible as an override — it must not silently discard a requested\n  capability's provenance.\n- `provenance` is explanatory/audit metadata, not an extra route key.\n- Work/workflow/task/skill objects never cross this boundary as semantic\n  resolver input; they are read by the component-outer caller only, before\n  a DispatchRequest is built.\n- An unavailable capability is a valid resolution result (`mechanism:\n  \"unavailable\"`), not malformed config.\n\n**Implementation status.** No single typed `DispatchRequest` object exists\nyet. `compileDispatchPlan()`'s options bag\n(`executorId | for | work | assignment | stage | needsSoul |\nhasLiveTaskAccess | caller | cliOverride | options`) is the de facto request\nshape today — untyped, and `work`/`assignment` are resolved to a\ncapability/executor-id *inside* `plan.mjs` rather than by the caller before\nthe boundary. Introducing a normalized `DispatchRequest` helper near\n`plan.mjs` without changing `compileDispatchPlan`'s role as the sole\nexecution chooser is Slice D scope.\n\n### PolicyPatch\n\nOne validated shape at every declared scope (runner/default, definition,\nnode, operation, role, actor, Work, Assignment, human/CLI, governance) — see\nthe [FlowDefinition Contract](../contracts/flow-definition.md#policypatch)\nfor the accepted schema. Dispatch does not define a second policy shape; it\nconsumes the same one.\n\n```txt\nrunner/default\n→ definition/protocol\n→ operation/taskSpec\n→ role\n→ actor/persona\n→ Work constraints\n→ Assignment\n→ trusted human/CLI override\n→ governance\n```\n\nMerge rules (already accepted and enforced):\n\n- tier constraints accumulate monotonically — a weaker layer cannot lower a\n  stronger required tier;\n- executor preference is most-specific-wins, subject to registration and\n  governance;\n- provider family derives from the selected registered executor, never from\n  a raw selector string;\n- literal model/executor names are not portable workflow/protocol data — a\n  *portable* definition expresses `minTier`/`capabilities` only;\n- provenance records the winning scope for every resolved field, as\n  `{field: {value, source: {scope, id}}}`.\n\n**Implementation status.** Implemented. `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy()`\n(`src/runner/dispatch/assignment-policy.mjs`) implements this exact\nprecedence and provenance shape. `assertNoPortableExecutorPin()`\n(`src/runner/coordination/session-engine.mjs`) already rejects a literal\n`preferExecutor` declared at a portable definition/role/actor/operation\nscope. `fallbackExecutors` remains `reserved-not-executed`: recorded and\nvalidated, never automatically dispatched as failover.\n\n### DispatchPlan (core → runtime)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"requestedTarget\": { \"kind\": \"capability\", \"value\": \"code:implement\" },\n  \"requestedCapability\": \"code:implement\",\n  \"selectedExecutor\": \"agy-herdr\",\n  \"bindingSource\": \"capability.prefer\",\n  \"providerModel\": \"gemini\",\n  \"tier\": \"standard\",\n  \"model\": \"<resolved-from-policy>\",\n  \"mechanism\": \"out-of-process\",\n  \"invocation\": { \"via\": \"cli\", \"adapter\": \"herdr-spawn\" },\n  \"governance\": {},\n  \"provenance\": {}\n}\n```\n\nAn explicit executor override remains visible as an override; it must not\nsilently replace the requested capability's own provenance.\n\n**Implementation status.** Implemented for dispatchable plans.\n`compileDispatchPlan()` (`src/runner/dispatch/plan.mjs`) returns the legacy\nselector/mechanism fields plus `bindingSource`, `tier`, `model`,\n`providerModel`, structured field-level `provenance`, and the complete\nmerged `policy`. It delegates those policy fields to\n`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy()` rather than re-deriving them, and\n`assignment-runner.mjs` now reads `compiledPlan.policy` directly instead of\ncalling the policy resolver a second time.\n\nFor a real Assignment, policy resolution failure or a\ndecided-executor-versus-policy-executor mismatch remains a hard\n`RunnerConfigError`. For a non-Assignment compatibility request\n(`decide --for`, `decide <executor-id>`, `decide --work`), `plan.mjs`\nsynthesizes the smallest policy object needed for observability:\n`preferExecutor` is the already-selected executor, and capability\n`overrides.providerModel`/`overrides.model`/`overrides.tier`/\n`overrides.rigorOverrides` are folded into the synthesized policy so the\nreported model/tier matches the same capability-default path used by\nexecution. If that synthesized policy would disagree with an explicit caller\noverride, the plan stays dispatchable and records\n`policy.executor-mismatch-ignored`; the optional policy fields are left\nunset rather than turning a legacy `decide` probe into a thrown error.\n\nGovernance-blocked and genuinely unavailable plans also leave\n`tier`/`model`/`providerModel`/`provenance`/`policy` unset so they never\npublish a partial policy for a Run that will not launch.\n\n`selector.type: 'purpose'` in the current implementation corresponds to\n`requestedTarget.kind: 'capability'` in the target contract above (see\nRouting Identities). It is a compatibility label on the public shape, not a\nsemantic third identity.\n\n## Executor Kinds\n\nAn executor is not assumed to be an agent. `runner.executors.<id>.kind` is\none of `agent | tool` (`src/runner/dispatch/config.mjs`,\n`EXECUTOR_KINDS`) — orthogonal to the invocation mechanism\n(`invocations[].via`, one of `cli | task | mcp | api`). A `tool`/MCP-only\nexecutor (e.g. `gitnexus`, `invocations: [{via: \"mcp\"}]`) is never spawned\nas a subprocess: `resolveExecutorConfig()`'s own Gate B3 throws rather than\nsilently falling through to the global CLI executor when a caller asks an\nMCP-only executor to resolve for CLI dispatch. This is how impact-analysis\ntools like GitNexus participate in dispatch as executors without pretending\nto be agents — the same control plane, the same capability/executor-id\nrouting, a different declared mechanism.\n\n## Component-Internal Ownership\n\nThe Dispatch And Execution Engine owns exactly these authorities. No other\ncomponent performs any of them; this control plane performs none of the\nComponent-Outer Boundary Note's responsibilities.\n\n1. **Request normalizer** — accepts only a normalized capability/executor\n   target plus PolicyPatch/provenance; performs no Work graph traversal.\n2. **Capability binding resolver** — resolves capability aliases, `prefer`,\n   and executor `for[]` declarations (`resolveExecutorAndOverrides`).\n3. **Executor registry resolver** — resolves a literal executor-id to its\n   concrete invocation/tool/agent shape (`resolveExecutorConfig`).\n4. **Policy resolver** — `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`/\n   `mergePolicyStack`; owns provider/model/tier derivation and provenance.\n5. **Governance resolver** — checks egress/provider/executor/content\n   constraints (cross-provider gate, `allowCrossProvider`, `carries`).\n6. **Mechanism resolver** — decides in-process/out-of-process/unavailable\n   and MCP/tool handback (`decideDispatchMechanism`,\n   `decideExecutorDispatchMechanism`).\n7. **DispatchPlan compiler** — `compileDispatchPlan()`; joins the prior\n   decisions into one plan. Remains the sole execution chooser.\n8. **Run runtime/adapters** — creates, launches, observes, settles, and\n   retries a Run without choosing semantic operation\n   (`assignment-runner.mjs`, `transport.mjs`, `herdr-round.mjs`).\n\nForbidden dependencies for all eight:\n\n- no `Work` lifecycle mutation (`pick`, `return`, `claim`, `take`): enforced by boundary grep tests (`test/runner/dispatch-reconciliation-import-graph.test.mjs`). Work driving orchestration lives exclusively in Work Driver (`src/runner/loop.mjs`, `src/runner/fanout-batch.mjs`);\n- no event store append (`appendEvent`): audit dispatch logging is isolated to `src/runner/dispatch-log.mjs` outside dispatch core;\n- no workflow/stage/task/skill lookup: dispatch core contains no Work lookup implementations. Work capability lookups (`executorIdForWork`, `resolveCapabilityIdentityDetails`, `resolveCapabilityIdentity`, `buildPrompt`) are housed in dedicated leaf compatibility module `src/runner/work-compat.mjs` (registered as `infra` in architecture manifest) with zero imports into dispatch core; `src/runner/dispatch/resolve.mjs` and `prepare.mjs` provide backward-compatible re-exports without importing `workflow-stage-graphs` or `operation-choice.mjs`, consumed by pre-existing callers (`plan.mjs` for `compileDispatchPlan({work})` and `cli.mjs` for `spawnWorker`). All 13 strictly decoupled dispatch core modules contain zero `workflow-stage-graphs` imports, and boundary tests enforce that strict core modules cannot import Work lookup symbols or `work-compat.mjs` (verified by `test/runner/dispatch-reconciliation-import-graph.test.mjs`);\n- no semantic operation choice;\n- no direct protocol/skill/domain executor launch;\n- no RunResult confidence decision (owned by the Run Result Evaluator);\n- no provider/model selection outside the policy resolver (item 4);\n- no second private dispatch path for a coordination or domain harness —\n  `cohort-planner.mjs` is the one confirmed exception, and it only *re-reads*\n  `resolveExecutorConfig`/`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` for a\n  pre-dispatch feasibility check; it never spawns and never bypasses them.\n\n## Component-Outer Boundary Note\n\nWork Driver, Coordination Engine/FlowDefinition, Domain Harness, and\nHost/CLI/API callers derive a capability or explicit executor-id plus a\nPolicyPatch and provenance, then hand a DispatchRequest to this control\nplane. None of them calls `resolveExecutorConfig` or launches an executor\ndirectly. `dispatchDeclaredOperation()`\n(`src/runner/coordination/session-engine.mjs`) is the concrete example\ntoday: it composes a full scoped policy stack (runner → definition →\noperation → role → actor) and passes the winning provenance to\n`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` via `cliOverride.policyProvenance`, rather\nthan re-deriving policy itself. Full component-outer ownership (Work Driver,\nFlowDefinition/operation, domain harness, host CLI/API selector\ncompatibility) is documented in the normalization plan's Slice C scope, not\nduplicated here.\n\n## Governance\n\n- Executor identifiers must resolve through configured/approved targets.\n- Cross-provider/model/tier dispatch must remain explicit and auditable.\n- Capability, role, soul/profile, privacy, and context-egress requirements must\n  be resolved through policy rather than hard-wired to a Workflow.\n- CLI spawn is an execution mechanism, not a governance bypass.\n- Read-only/mutating policy must be checked before launch.\n- Result and artifact locations must be bounded and attributable to the Run.\n- Direct executor calls from protocol, Skill, coordinator, or domain-harness\n  prose are invalid.\n\n## Separation Of Concerns\n\n```txt\nplanner     proposes a declared or dynamic semantic action\npolicy      validates legality, authority, bounds, and selected domain rules\nbuilder     creates Assignment\nresolver    produces governed DispatchPlan\ndispatcher  launches and observes Run\nnormalizer  creates RunResult\ncaller      consumes evidence and invokes authorized lifecycle behavior, if any\n```\n\nPlanning may be agent-led, declared, or domain-assisted. Dispatch does not care\nwhich source proposed the validated Assignment and must not create separate\nruntime paths for them. No other name\nresolves a Run target.\n\n```txt\ncapability   — abstract behavior promise, resolved through\n               runner.capabilities.<capability> (prefer/overrides), then\n               runner.executors.<id>.for[] (kind \"tool\" executors only)\nexecutor-id  — explicit concrete implementation override, naming a\n               runner.executors.<id> entry directly\n```\n\n`purpose` is not a third identity. It is compatibility terminology for\ncapability. The `--for <purpose>` CLI flag and the `purpose`/`for` parameter\nnames threaded through `src/runner/dispatch/plan.mjs` and\n`src/runner/dispatch/resolve.mjs` (`resolveExecutorIdForPurpose`,\n`resolveExecutorAndOverrides(cfg, executorIdOrPurpose)`) all name a capability\nvalue, resolved against the same `runner.capabilities` catalog an explicit\ncapability selector would use. `compileDispatchPlan()`'s\n`selector.type: 'purpose'` denotes a capability-shaped request, not a separate\nontology; nothing downstream branches on `purpose` as a concept distinct from\ncapability. Renaming these call sites internally is compatibility work\n(tracked as Slice D/E in the normalization plan above), not a semantic\nchange — `--for` and `--work` stay supported on `decide` at the CLI/API\nadapter layer. (`execute --assignment` was removed with the rest of the raw\n`dispatch execute` door, decision 0062 in `docs/specs/runner.md`; work runs\nthrough `fgos run`.)\n\n`job` is not a routing identity. ADR-004 reserves the term for a possible\nfuture scheduler; where it appears (e.g. in logs), it names a caller's\nexecution-request label, never a target this control plane resolves against.\nA `Run` (see the [Assignment/Run/RunResult Contract](../contracts/assignment-run-runresult.md))\nis one concrete execution attempt for an Assignment — it is not a job or\noperation identity either.\n\nWork, workflow, stage, operation, taskSpec, skill, and protocol context are\ncomponent-outer. A caller in that layer may derive a capability or an\nexplicit executor-id from them before entering this control plane; none of\nthem becomes a third resolvable identity inside dispatch core. See\nComponent-Outer Boundary Note below.\n\n## Contracts\n\nThese three contracts are canonical for this control plane. They are\nadditive over the current implementation, not a replacement of it — see the\nImplementation Status line under each for what is real today versus still\nSlice D/E scope in the normalization plan.\n\n### DispatchRequest (outer → core)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"target\": { \"kind\": \"capability | executor\", \"value\": \"code:implement\" },\n  \"policy\": {\n    \"minTier\": \"standard\",\n    \"preferExecutor\": \"agy-herdr\",\n    \"fallbackExecutors\": [\"codex-herdr\"],\n    \"preferPersona\": \"code-reviewer\",\n    \"visibility\": \"headless\"\n  },\n  \"provenance\": {\n    \"source\": \"workflow-operation\",\n    \"domain\": \"coding\",\n    \"workflow\": \"feature\",\n    \"stage\": \"executing\",\n    \"operation\": \"implement-item\",\n    \"taskSpec\": \"implement-item\",\n    \"skill\": \"fgos-coding-implement\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- `target.kind: capability` resolves through `runner.capabilities` and\n  executor `for[]` bindings.\n- `target.kind: executor` is an explicit concrete override and remains\n  visible as an override — it must not silently discard a requested\n  capability's provenance.\n- `provenance` is explanatory/audit metadata, not an extra route key.\n- Work/workflow/task/skill objects never cross this boundary as semantic\n  resolver input; they are read by the component-outer caller only, before\n  a DispatchRequest is built.\n- An unavailable capability is a valid resolution result (`mechanism:\n  \"unavailable\"`), not malformed config.\n\n**Implementation status.** No single typed `DispatchRequest` object exists\nyet. `compileDispatchPlan()`'s options bag\n(`executorId | for | work | assignment | stage | needsSoul |\nhasLiveTaskAccess | caller | cliOverride | options`) is the de facto request\nshape today — untyped, and `work`/`assignment` are resolved to a\ncapability/executor-id *inside* `plan.mjs` rather than by the caller before\nthe boundary. Introducing a normalized `DispatchRequest` helper near\n`plan.mjs` without changing `compileDispatchPlan`'s role as the sole\nexecution chooser is Slice D scope.\n\n### PolicyPatch\n\nOne validated shape at every declared scope (runner/default, definition,\nnode, operation, role, actor, Work, Assignment, human/CLI, governance) — see\nthe [FlowDefinition Contract](../contracts/flow-definition.md#policypatch)\nfor the accepted schema. Dispatch does not define a second policy shape; it\nconsumes the same one.\n\n```txt\nrunner/default\n→ definition/protocol\n→ operation/taskSpec\n→ role\n→ actor/persona\n→ Work constraints\n→ Assignment\n→ trusted human/CLI override\n→ governance\n```\n\nMerge rules (already accepted and enforced):\n\n- tier constraints accumulate monotonically — a weaker layer cannot lower a\n  stronger required tier;\n- executor preference is most-specific-wins, subject to registration and\n  governance;\n- provider family derives from the selected registered executor, never from\n  a raw selector string;\n- literal model/executor names are not portable workflow/protocol data — a\n  *portable* definition expresses `minTier`/`capabilities` only;\n- provenance records the winning scope for every resolved field, as\n  `{field: {value, source: {scope, id}}}`.\n\n**Implementation status.** Implemented. `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy()`\n(`src/runner/dispatch/assignment-policy.mjs`) implements this exact\nprecedence and provenance shape. `assertNoPortableExecutorPin()`\n(`src/runner/coordination/session-engine.mjs`) already rejects a literal\n`preferExecutor` declared at a portable definition/role/actor/operation\nscope. `fallbackExecutors` remains `reserved-not-executed`: recorded and\nvalidated, never automatically dispatched as failover.\n\n### DispatchPlan (core → runtime)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"requestedTarget\": { \"kind\": \"capability\", \"value\": \"code:implement\" },\n  \"requestedCapability\": \"code:implement\",\n  \"selectedExecutor\": \"agy-herdr\",\n  \"bindingSource\": \"capability.prefer\",\n  \"providerModel\": \"gemini\",\n  \"tier\": \"standard\",\n  \"model\": \"<resolved-from-policy>\",\n  \"mechanism\": \"out-of-process\",\n  \"invocation\": { \"via\": \"cli\", \"adapter\": \"herdr-spawn\" },\n  \"governance\": {},\n  \"provenance\": {}\n}\n```\n\nAn explicit executor override remains visible as an override; it must not\nsilently replace the requested capability's own provenance.\n\n**Implementation status.** Implemented for dispatchable plans.\n`compileDispatchPlan()` (`src/runner/dispatch/plan.mjs`) returns the legacy\nselector/mechanism fields plus `bindingSource`, `tier`, `model`,\n`providerModel`, structured field-level `provenance`, and the complete\nmerged `policy`. It delegates those policy fields to\n`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy()` rather than re-deriving them, and\n`assignment-runner.mjs` now reads `compiledPlan.policy` directly instead of\ncalling the policy resolver a second time.\n\nFor a real Assignment, policy resolution failure or a\ndecided-executor-versus-policy-executor mismatch remains a hard\n`RunnerConfigError`. For a non-Assignment compatibility request\n(`decide --for`, `decide <executor-id>`, `decide --work`), `plan.mjs`\nsynthesizes the smallest policy object needed for observability:\n`preferExecutor` is the already-selected executor, and capability\n`overrides.providerModel`/`overrides.model`/`overrides.tier`/\n`overrides.rigorOverrides` are folded into the synthesized policy so the\nreported model/tier matches the same capability-default path used by\nexecution. If that synthesized policy would disagree with an explicit caller\noverride, the plan stays dispatchable and records\n`policy.executor-mismatch-ignored`; the optional policy fields are left\nunset rather than turning a legacy `decide` probe into a thrown error.\n\nGovernance-blocked and genuinely unavailable plans also leave\n`tier`/`model`/`providerModel`/`provenance`/`policy` unset so they never\npublish a partial policy for a Run that will not launch.\n\n`selector.type: 'purpose'` in the current implementation corresponds to\n`requestedTarget.kind: 'capability'` in the target contract above (see\nRouting Identities). It is a compatibility label on the public shape, not a\nsemantic third identity.\n\n## Executor Kinds\n\nAn executor is not assumed to be an agent. `runner.executors.<id>.kind` is\none of `agent | tool` (`src/runner/dispatch/config.mjs`,\n`EXECUTOR_KINDS`) — orthogonal to the invocation mechanism\n(`invocations[].via`, one of `cli | task | mcp | api`). A `tool`/MCP-only\nexecutor (e.g. `gitnexus`, `invocations: [{via: \"mcp\"}]`) is never spawned\nas a subprocess: `resolveExecutorConfig()`'s own Gate B3 throws rather than\nsilently falling through to the global CLI executor when a caller asks an\nMCP-only executor to resolve for CLI dispatch. This is how impact-analysis\ntools like GitNexus participate in dispatch as executors without pretending\nto be agents — the same control plane, the same capability/executor-id\nrouting, a different declared mechanism.\n\n## Component-Internal Ownership\n\nThe Dispatch And Execution Engine owns exactly these authorities. No other\ncomponent performs any of them; this control plane performs none of the\nComponent-Outer Boundary Note's responsibilities.\n\n1. **Request normalizer** — accepts only a normalized capability/executor\n   target plus PolicyPatch/provenance; performs no Work graph traversal.\n2. **Capability binding resolver** — resolves capability aliases, `prefer`,\n   and executor `for[]` declarations (`resolveExecutorAndOverrides`).\n3. **Executor registry resolver** — resolves a literal executor-id to its\n   concrete invocation/tool/agent shape (`resolveExecutorConfig`).\n4. **Policy resolver** — `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`/\n   `mergePolicyStack`; owns provider/model/tier derivation and provenance.\n5. **Governance resolver** — checks egress/provider/executor/content\n   constraints (cross-provider gate, `allowCrossProvider`, `carries`).\n6. **Mechanism resolver** — decides in-process/out-of-process/unavailable\n   and MCP/tool handback (`decideDispatchMechanism`,\n   `decideExecutorDispatchMechanism`).\n7. **DispatchPlan compiler** — `compileDispatchPlan()`; joins the prior\n   decisions into one plan. Remains the sole execution chooser.\n8. **Run runtime/adapters** — creates, launches, observes, settles, and\n   retries a Run without choosing semantic operation\n   (`assignment-runner.mjs`, `transport.mjs`, `herdr-round.mjs`).\n\nForbidden dependencies for all eight:\n\n- no `Work` lifecycle mutation (`pick`, `return`, `claim`, `take`): enforced by boundary grep tests (`test/runner/dispatch-reconciliation-import-graph.test.mjs`). Work driving orchestration lives exclusively in Work Driver (`src/runner/loop.mjs`, `src/runner/fanout-batch.mjs`);\n- no event store append (`appendEvent`): audit dispatch logging was isolated to `src/runner/dispatch-log.mjs` outside dispatch core (module removed with `dispatch log`, decision 0062; `fgos run` records provenance under `.fgos/assignments/<unitRunId>/`);\n- no workflow/stage/task/skill lookup: dispatch core contains no Work lookup implementations. Work capability lookups (`executorIdForWork`, `resolveCapabilityIdentityDetails`, `resolveCapabilityIdentity`, `buildPrompt`) are housed in dedicated leaf compatibility module `src/runner/work-compat.mjs` (registered as `infra` in architecture manifest) with zero imports into dispatch core; `src/runner/dispatch/resolve.mjs` and `prepare.mjs` provide backward-compatible re-exports without importing `workflow-stage-graphs` or `operation-choice.mjs`, consumed by pre-existing callers (`plan.mjs` for `compileDispatchPlan({work})` and `cli.mjs` for `spawnWorker`). All 13 strictly decoupled dispatch core modules contain zero `workflow-stage-graphs` imports, and boundary tests enforce that strict core modules cannot import Work lookup symbols or `work-compat.mjs` (verified by `test/runner/dispatch-reconciliation-import-graph.test.mjs`);\n- no semantic operation choice;\n- no direct protocol/skill/domain executor launch;\n- no RunResult confidence decision (owned by the Run Result Evaluator);\n- no provider/model selection outside the policy resolver (item 4);\n- no second private dispatch path for a coordination or domain harness —\n  `cohort-planner.mjs` is the one confirmed exception, and it only *re-reads*\n  `resolveExecutorConfig`/`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` for a\n  pre-dispatch feasibility check; it never spawns and never bypasses them.\n\n## Component-Outer Boundary Note\n\nWork Driver, Coordination Engine/FlowDefinition, Domain Harness, and\nHost/CLI/API callers derive a capability or explicit executor-id plus a\nPolicyPatch and provenance, then hand a DispatchRequest to this control\nplane. None of them calls `resolveExecutorConfig` or launches an executor\ndirectly. `dispatchDeclaredOperation()`\n(`src/runner/coordination/session-engine.mjs`) is the concrete example\ntoday: it composes a full scoped policy stack (runner → definition →\noperation → role → actor) and passes the winning provenance to\n`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` via `cliOverride.policyProvenance`, rather\nthan re-deriving policy itself. Full component-outer ownership (Work Driver,\nFlowDefinition/operation, domain harness, host CLI/API selector\ncompatibility) is documented in the normalization plan's Slice C scope, not\nduplicated here.\n\n## Governance\n\n- Executor identifiers must resolve through configured/approved targets.\n- Cross-provider/model/tier dispatch must remain explicit and auditable.\n- Capability, role, soul/profile, privacy, and context-egress requirements must\n  be resolved through policy rather than hard-wired to a Workflow.\n- CLI spawn is an execution mechanism, not a governance bypass.\n- Read-only/mutating policy must be checked before launch.\n- Result and artifact locations must be bounded and attributable to the Run.\n- Direct executor calls from protocol, Skill, coordinator, or domain-harness\n  prose are invalid.\n\n## Separation Of Concerns\n\n```txt\nplanner     proposes a declared or dynamic semantic action\npolicy      validates legality, authority, bounds, and selected domain rules\nbuilder     creates Assignment\nresolver    produces governed DispatchPlan\ndispatcher  launches and observes Run\nnormalizer  creates RunResult\ncaller      consumes evidence and invokes authorized lifecycle behavior, if any\n```\n\nPlanning may be agent-led, declared, or domain-assisted. Dispatch does not care\nwhich source proposed the validated Assignment and must not create separate\nruntime paths for them. A CoordinationSession or a declared\n`CoordinationProtocol` FlowDefinition (see\n[ADR-008](../decisions/ADR-008-coordination-session-and-mission-deferral.md),\n[ADR-009](../decisions/ADR-009-flow-definition-shared-ir-and-typed-profiles.md))\nis one more caller of this same flow: a Cohort Planner may emit actor policy\ninputs, but it resolves and dispatches exactly one Assignment at a time\nthrough this control plane — it may not spawn an executor directly or read\nsibling Assignment state.\n\nThe detailed redesign source remains a\n[proposal](../proposals/dispatch-control-plane-redesign.md) until its unresolved\ntarget-state sections are reconciled with implementation.\n\n## Source Inventory\n\n| Layer | Modules | Responsibilities & Boundaries |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Dispatch Core | `src/runner/dispatch/**` (`cli.mjs`, `plan.mjs`, `resolve.mjs`, `prepare.mjs`, `settlement.mjs`, `reconcile-cli-spawn.mjs`, `herdr-reconcile.mjs`, `proof-helpers.mjs`, `assignment-runner.mjs`, `confinement/**`, `transport.mjs`, `herdr-round.mjs`, `brief.mjs`, `assignment.mjs`, `runtime-inspection.mjs`) | Execution allocation, plan compilation, executor commands, confinement, and adapter execution. ## Responsibility

The dispatch control plane converts one semantic Assignment into one governed
execution attempt. It resolves target, capability, provider/model/tier,
soul/profile, mechanism, adapter, policy checks, result channel, and runtime
metadata.

It does not choose the Work lifecycle transition or invent a semantic operation.

## Flow

```txt
Assignment
  -> policy resolver
  -> executor/target resolution
  -> governance and egress checks
  -> mechanism/adapter selection
  -> execution capability set
  -> Run creation and launch
  -> settlement/result collection
  -> RunResult normalization
```

Execution requirements are not inferred merely from the mechanism name.
The current implementation expresses prompt delivery, permission posture and
confinement through executor/configuration and adapter checks. A unified
`execution capability set` is a design description, not a separately emitted
plan field or an implemented compiler stage. Unsupported requirements must
not be silently weakened; check the owning adapter and confinement authority.

## Routing Identities

The dispatch core recognizes exactly two target identities. No other name
resolves a Run target.

```txt
capability   — abstract behavior promise, resolved through
               runner.capabilities.<capability> (prefer/overrides), then
               runner.executors.<id>.for[] (kind "tool" executors only)
executor-id  — explicit concrete implementation override, naming a
               runner.executors.<id> entry directly
```

`purpose` is not a third identity. It is compatibility terminology for
capability. The `--for <purpose>` CLI flag and the `purpose`/`for` parameter
names threaded through `src/runner/dispatch/plan.mjs` and
`src/runner/dispatch/resolve.mjs` (`resolveExecutorAndOverrides`) name capability
values. `resolveExecutorIdForPurpose` is not a current exported resolver.
`compileDispatchPlan()`'s `selector.type: 'purpose'` is the compatibility
selector label. It does not create a third conceptual route identity.
The [earlier normalization plan](../../../history/dispatch-core-contract-normalization/plan.md)
is dated migration context, not an assertion that its remaining helpers ship.

`job` is not a routing identity. ADR-004 reserves the term for a possible
future scheduler; where it appears (e.g. in logs), it names a caller's
execution-request label, never a target this control plane resolves against.
A `Run` (see the [Assignment/Run/RunResult Contract](../contracts/assignment-run-runresult.md))
is one concrete execution attempt for an Assignment — it is not a job or
operation identity either.

Work, workflow, stage, operation, taskSpec, skill, and protocol context are
component-outer. A caller in that layer may derive a capability or an
explicit executor-id from them before entering this control plane; none of
them becomes a third resolvable identity inside dispatch core. See
Component-Outer Boundary Note below.

## Contracts

The following shapes describe the intended request/policy/plan boundary.
The status below each distinguishes design fields from the actual exported
function inputs and compiled output; do not send the illustrative JSON as if
all fields were already accepted by a typed normalizer.

### DispatchRequest (outer → core)

```json
{
  "target": { "kind": "capability | executor", "value": "code:implement" },
  "policy": {
    "rigor": "standard",
    "preferExecutor": "agy-herdr",
    "fallbackExecutors": ["codex-herdr"],
    "preferPersona": "code-reviewer",
    "visibility": "headless"
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "workflow-operation",
    "domain": "coding",
    "workflow": "feature",
    "workflowStep": "executing",
    "operation": "implement-item",
    "taskSpec": "implement-item",
    "skill": "fgos-coding-implement"
  }
}
```

Rules:

- `target.kind: capability` resolves through `runner.capabilities` and
  executor `for[]` bindings.
- `target.kind: executor` is an explicit concrete override and remains
  visible as an override — it must not silently discard a requested
  capability's provenance.
- `provenance` is explanatory/audit metadata, not an extra route key.
- Work/workflow/task/skill objects never cross this boundary as semantic
  resolver input; they are read by the component-outer caller only, before
  a DispatchRequest is built.
- An unavailable capability is a valid resolution result (`mechanism:
  "unavailable"`), not malformed config.

**Implementation status.** No single typed `DispatchRequest` object exists
yet. `compileDispatchPlan()`'s options bag
(`executorId | for | work | assignment | needsSoul | hasLiveTaskAccess |
caller | workItem | workExecutorId | assignmentItem | cliOverride | options`)
is the current input shape (`plan.mjs:46-60`). Work compatibility context is
resolved through that path, not through a shipped typed DispatchRequest helper.
The proposed normalized outer request remains an unimplemented design.

### PolicyPatch

```txt
Global defaults
→ Domain defaults
→ Workflow defaults
→ Step defaults
→ Operation/taskSpec defaults
→ Role defaults
→ Persona defaults
→ Work policy
→ Assignment policy
→ Human/CLI inputs
→ Governance
```

This is the documented policy composition order, not a claim that every scope
is separately discovered by the leaf resolver. Callers supply composed inputs;
`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` resolves Assignment/Work/config/caller inputs.

- Explicit rigor requirements cannot be weakened by a later lower requirement;
  the implicit standard is a fallback, not a floor. Derived tiers retain the
  strongest requirement (`assignment-policy.mjs:224-325`).
- Executor/persona preferences use the most-specific supported input, subject
  to governance (`assignment-policy.mjs:332-380`).
- Provider/model selection belongs to the registered executor/policy path.
- Portable YAML uses rigor rather than removed `minTier` or explicit tier/model
  pins; the resolver rejects those retired/forbidden inputs
  (`assignment-policy.mjs:203-215`). A general
  `assertNoPortableExecutorPin` helper is not current implementation.
- Effective provenance records winning values and sources
  (`assignment-policy.mjs:493-505`); no current `mergePolicyStack` function is
  implied by the composition diagram.

### DispatchPlan (core → runtime)

```json
{
  "requestedTarget": { "kind": "capability", "value": "code:implement" },
  "requestedCapability": "code:implement",
  "selectedExecutor": "agy-herdr",
  "bindingSource": "capability.prefer",
  "providerModel": "gemini",
  "tier": "standard",
  "model": "<resolved-from-policy>",
  "mechanism": "out-of-process",
  "invocation": { "via": "cli", "adapter": "herdr-spawn" },
  "governance": {},
  "provenance": {}
}
```

An explicit executor override remains visible as an override; it must not
silently replace the requested capability's own provenance.

**Implementation status.** The illustrative `requestedTarget`,
`requestedCapability` and `selectedExecutor` names above are target-state
vocabulary, not current compiled output keys. `compileDispatchPlan()` returns
`selector`, `caller`, `mechanism`, `executorId`, `capability`, `invocation`,
`governance`, `reasonCodes`, optional `agentType`/`mcpTool`, `configured`,
`bindingSource`, `tier`, `model`, `providerModel`, `provenance` and `policy`
(`plan.mjs:444-461`). Policy resolution delegates to
`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`; it is not duplicated by the caller.

For a real Assignment, policy resolution failure or a
decided-executor-versus-policy-executor mismatch remains a hard
`RunnerConfigError`. For a non-Assignment compatibility request
(`decide --for`, `decide <executor-id>`, `decide --work`), `plan.mjs`
synthesizes an Assignment policy with `preferExecutor` and, when configured,
capability `rigor` and `capability` (`plan.mjs:403-411`).
Removed capability `overrides` are rejected by config validation, not folded
into policy. Synthetic policy failures leave policy fields null; an executor
mismatch also records `policy.executor-mismatch-ignored`
(`plan.mjs:422-441`). A real Assignment's corresponding failure remains fatal.

Governance-blocked and genuinely unavailable plans also leave
`tier`/`model`/`providerModel`/`provenance`/`policy` unset so they never
publish a partial policy for a Run that will not launch.

`selector.type: 'purpose'` in the current implementation corresponds to
`requestedTarget.kind: 'capability'` in the target contract above (see
Routing Identities). It is a compatibility label on the public shape, not a
semantic third identity.

## Executor Kinds

An executor is not assumed to be an agent. `runner.executors.<id>.kind` is
one of `agent | tool` (`src/runner/dispatch/config.mjs`,
`EXECUTOR_KINDS`) — orthogonal to the invocation mechanism
(`invocations[].via`, one of `cli | task | mcp | api`). A `tool`/MCP-only
executor (e.g. `gitnexus`, `invocations: [{via: "mcp"}]`) is never spawned
as a subprocess: `resolveExecutorConfig()`'s own Gate B3 throws rather than
silently falling through to the global CLI executor when a caller asks an
MCP-only executor to resolve for CLI dispatch. This is how impact-analysis
tools like GitNexus participate in dispatch as executors without pretending
to be agents — the same control plane, the same capability/executor-id
routing, a different declared mechanism.

## Component-Internal Ownership

The Dispatch And Execution Engine owns exactly these authorities. No other
component performs any of them; this control plane performs none of the
Component-Outer Boundary Note's responsibilities.

1. **Request normalizer (design)** — the normalized target/policy/provenance
   boundary is proposed; current inputs are the compiler options above.
2. **Capability binding resolver** — `resolveExecutorAndOverrides` binds literal
   executor IDs/defaults or capability `prefer`; aliases and executor `for[]`
   inform capability labels separately in `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints`
   (`resolve.mjs:25-66,269-310`), not this binding resolver.
3. **Executor registry resolver** — resolves a literal executor-id to its
   concrete invocation/tool/agent shape (`resolveExecutorConfig`).
4. **Policy resolver** — `resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`; owns supported
   provider/model/rigor/tier derivation and provenance, not a `mergePolicyStack`.
5. **Governance resolver** — checks egress/provider/executor/content
   constraints (cross-provider gate, `allowCrossProvider`, `carries`).
6. **Mechanism resolver** — decides in-process/out-of-process/unavailable
   and MCP/tool handback (`decideDispatchMechanism`,
   `decideExecutorDispatchMechanism`).
7. **DispatchPlan compiler** — `compileDispatchPlan()` joins the legacy
   dispatch decisions. Unit execution first obtains its binding through
   `bind()`; assignment-runner revalidates that binding and compiles the
   governed execution plan. The domain harness owns neither choice.
8. **Run runtime/adapters** — creates, launches, observes, settles, and
   retries a Run without choosing semantic operation
   (`assignment-runner.mjs`, `transport.mjs`, `herdr-round.mjs`).

Forbidden dependencies for all eight:

- no `Work` lifecycle mutation (`pick`, `return`, `claim`, `take`): enforced by boundary grep tests (`test/runner/dispatch-reconciliation-import-graph.test.mjs`). Work driving orchestration lives exclusively in Work Driver (`src/runner/loop.mjs`, `src/runner/fanout-batch.mjs`);
- no event store append (`appendEvent`): audit dispatch logging is isolated to `src/runner/dispatch-log.mjs` outside dispatch core;
- no semantic Workflow/domain operation lookup in the strictly decoupled dispatch core. Work-layer lookups belong to `src/runner/work-compat.mjs` and `src/runner/operation-choice.mjs`; caller-derived hints enter the compiler. Historical compatibility re-exports and an `infra` manifest label are not current ownership proof. See boundary tests at `test/runner/dispatch-reconciliation-import-graph.test.mjs:434-443`.
- no semantic operation choice;
- no direct protocol/skill/domain executor launch;
- no RunResult confidence decision (owned by the Run Result Evaluator);
- no provider/model selection outside the policy resolver (item 4);
- no second private executor-launch path for a domain or coordinating harness.
  The retired `cohort-planner.mjs` is not a current exception or authority.

## Component-Outer Boundary Note

Work, host, CLI/API and domain callers choose the semantic task and pass its
target/capability, policy inputs and provenance into governed execution.
They retain lifecycle decisions and consume returned evidence; they must not
resolve executor configuration and launch around dispatch governance or
confinement. The proposed outer normalizer is not a shipped alternate door.

## Governance

- Executor identifiers must resolve through configured/approved targets.
- Cross-provider/model/tier dispatch must remain explicit and auditable.
- Capability, role, soul/profile, privacy, and context-egress requirements must
  be resolved through policy rather than hard-wired to a Workflow.
- CLI spawn is an execution mechanism, not a governance bypass.
- Read-only/mutating policy must be checked before launch.
- Result and artifact locations must be bounded and attributable to the Run.
- Direct executor calls from protocol, Skill, coordinator, or domain-harness
  prose are invalid.

## Separation Of Concerns

Planning may be agent-led, declared by a Workflow, or supplied by a domain
harness. A validated Assignment still enters the same governed execution path;
the planning source does not grant a private launch or result-acceptance path.

```txt
planner     proposes a declared or dynamic semantic action
policy      validates legality, authority, bounds, and selected domain rules
builder     creates Assignment
resolver    produces governed DispatchPlan
dispatcher  launches and observes Run
normalizer  creates RunResult
caller      consumes evidence and invokes authorized lifecycle behavior, if any
```

The detailed redesign source remains a
[proposal](../proposals/dispatch-control-plane-redesign.md) until its unresolved
target-state sections are reconciled with implementation.

Boundary tests prohibit Work lifecycle mutation/imports; they do not prohibit every textual occurrence of `claim`. |

| Audit Seam | `src/runner/dispatch-log.mjs` | Audit event logging (`logExecutorDispatch`) isolated from dispatch core. |

## Responsibility

The dispatch control plane converts one semantic Assignment into one governed
execution attempt. It resolves target, capability, provider/model/tier,
soul/profile, mechanism, adapter, policy checks, result channel, and runtime
metadata.

It does not choose the Work lifecycle transition or invent a semantic operation.

## Flow

```txt
Assignment
  -> policy resolver
  -> executor/target resolution
  -> governance and egress checks
  -> mechanism/adapter selection
  -> execution capability set
  -> Run creation and launch
  -> settlement/result collection
  -> RunResult normalization
```

Execution requirements are not inferred merely from the mechanism name.
The current implementation expresses prompt delivery, permission posture and
confinement through executor/configuration and adapter checks. A unified
`execution capability set` is a design description, not a separately emitted
plan field or an implemented compiler stage. Unsupported requirements must
not be silently weakened; check the owning adapter and confinement authority.

## Routing Identities

The dispatch core recognizes exactly two target identities. No other name
resolves a Run target.

```txt
capability   — abstract behavior promise, resolved through
               runner.capabilities.<capability> (prefer/overrides), then
               runner.executors.<id>.for[] (kind "tool" executors only)
executor-id  — explicit concrete implementation override, naming a
               runner.executors.<id> entry directly
```

`purpose` is not a third identity. It is compatibility terminology for
capability. The `--for <purpose>` CLI flag and the `purpose`/`for` parameter
names threaded through `src/runner/dispatch/plan.mjs` and
`src/runner/dispatch/resolve.mjs` (`resolveExecutorAndOverrides`) name capability
values. `resolveExecutorIdForPurpose` is not a current exported resolver.
`compileDispatchPlan()`'s `selector.type: 'purpose'` is the compatibility
selector label. It does not create a third conceptual route identity.
`--for` and `--work` stay supported on `decide` at the CLI/API
adapter layer. (`execute --assignment` was removed with the rest of the raw
`dispatch execute` door, decision 0062 in `docs/specs/runner.md`; work runs
through `fgos run`.)
The [earlier normalization plan](../../../history/dispatch-core-contract-normalization/plan.md)
is dated migration context, not an assertion that its remaining helpers ship.

`job` is not a routing identity. ADR-004 reserves the term for a possible
future scheduler; where it appears (e.g. in logs), it names a caller's
execution-request label, never a target this control plane resolves against.
A `Run` (see the [Assignment/Run/RunResult Contract](../contracts/assignment-run-runresult.md))
is one concrete execution attempt for an Assignment — it is not a job or
operation identity either.

Work, workflow, stage, operation, taskSpec, skill, and protocol context are
component-outer. A caller in that layer may derive a capability or an
explicit executor-id from them before entering this control plane; none of
them becomes a third resolvable identity inside dispatch core. See
Component-Outer Boundary Note below.

## Contracts

The following shapes describe the intended request/policy/plan boundary.
The status below each distinguishes design fields from the actual exported
function inputs and compiled output; do not send the illustrative JSON as if
all fields were already accepted by a typed normalizer.

### DispatchRequest (outer → core)

```json
{
  "target": { "kind": "capability | executor", "value": "code:implement" },
  "policy": {
    "rigor": "standard",
    "preferExecutor": "agy-herdr",
    "fallbackExecutors": ["codex-herdr"],
    "preferPersona": "code-reviewer",
    "visibility": "headless"
  },
  "provenance": {
    "source": "workflow-operation",
    "domain": "coding",
    "workflow": "feature",
    "workflowStep": "executing",
    "operation": "implement-item",
    "taskSpec": "implement-item",
    "skill": "fgos-coding-implement"
  }
}
```

Rules:

- `target.kind: capability` resolves through `runner.capabilities` and
  executor `for[]` bindings.
- `target.kind: executor` is an explicit concrete override and remains
  visible as an override — it must not silently discard a requested
  capability's provenance.
- `provenance` is explanatory/audit metadata, not an extra route key.
- Work/workflow/task/skill objects never cross this boundary as semantic
  resolver input; they are read by the component-outer caller only, before
  a DispatchRequest is built.
- An unavailable capability is a valid resolution result (`mechanism:
  "unavailable"`), not malformed config.

**Implementation status.** No single typed `DispatchRequest` object exists
yet. `compileDispatchPlan()`'s options bag
(`executorId | for | work | assignment | needsSoul | hasLiveTaskAccess |
caller | workItem | workExecutorId | assignmentItem | cliOverride | options`)
is the current input shape (`plan.mjs:46-60`). Work compatibility context is
resolved through that path, not through a shipped typed DispatchRequest helper.
The proposed normalized outer request remains an unimplemented design.

### PolicyPatch

```txt
Global defaults
→ Domain defaults
→ Workflow defaults
→ Step defaults
→ Operation/taskSpec defaults
→ Role defaults
→ Persona defaults
→ Work policy
→ Assignment policy
→ Human/CLI inputs
→ Governance
```

This is the documented policy composition order, not a claim that every scope
is separately discovered by the leaf resolver. Callers supply composed inputs;
`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy` resolves Assignment/Work/config/caller inputs.

- Explicit rigor requirements cannot be weakened by a later lower requirement;
  the implicit standard is a fallback, not a floor. Derived tiers retain the
  strongest requirement (`assignment-policy.mjs:224-325`).
- Executor/persona preferences use the most-specific supported input, subject
  to governance (`assignment-policy.mjs:332-380`).
- Provider/model selection belongs to the registered executor/policy path.
- Portable YAML uses rigor rather than removed `minTier` or explicit tier/model
  pins; the resolver rejects those retired/forbidden inputs
  (`assignment-policy.mjs:203-215`). A general
  `assertNoPortableExecutorPin` helper is not current implementation.
- Effective provenance records winning values and sources
  (`assignment-policy.mjs:493-505`); no current `mergePolicyStack` function is
  implied by the composition diagram.

### DispatchPlan (core → runtime)

```json
{
  "requestedTarget": { "kind": "capability", "value": "code:implement" },
  "requestedCapability": "code:implement",
  "selectedExecutor": "agy-herdr",
  "bindingSource": "capability.prefer",
  "providerModel": "gemini",
  "tier": "standard",
  "model": "<resolved-from-policy>",
  "mechanism": "out-of-process",
  "invocation": { "via": "cli", "adapter": "herdr-spawn" },
  "governance": {},
  "provenance": {}
}
```

An explicit executor override remains visible as an override; it must not
silently replace the requested capability's own provenance.

**Implementation status.** The illustrative `requestedTarget`,
`requestedCapability` and `selectedExecutor` names above are target-state
vocabulary, not current compiled output keys. `compileDispatchPlan()` returns
`selector`, `caller`, `mechanism`, `executorId`, `capability`, `invocation`,
`governance`, `reasonCodes`, optional `agentType`/`mcpTool`, `configured`,
`bindingSource`, `tier`, `model`, `providerModel`, `provenance` and `policy`
(`plan.mjs:444-461`). Policy resolution delegates to
`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`; it is not duplicated by the caller.

For a real Assignment, policy resolution failure or a
decided-executor-versus-policy-executor mismatch remains a hard
`RunnerConfigError`. For a non-Assignment compatibility request
(`decide --for`, `decide <executor-id>`, `decide --work`), `plan.mjs`
synthesizes an Assignment policy with `preferExecutor` and, when configured,
capability `rigor` and `capability` (`plan.mjs:403-411`).
Removed capability `overrides` are rejected by config validation, not folded
into policy. Synthetic policy failures leave policy fields null; an executor
mismatch also records `policy.executor-mismatch-ignored`
(`plan.mjs:422-441`). A real Assignment's corresponding failure remains fatal.

Governance-blocked and genuinely unavailable plans also leave
`tier`/`model`/`providerModel`/`provenance`/`policy` unset so they never
publish a partial policy for a Run that will not launch.

`selector.type: 'purpose'` in the current implementation corresponds to
`requestedTarget.kind: 'capability'` in the target contract above (see
Routing Identities). It is a compatibility label on the public shape, not a
semantic third identity.

{
  "baseText": "# Architecture Advisory Coordinator Prompt\n\nDocument type: Playbook\nDesign status: N/A\nImplementation: Active (manual)\nLast reviewed: 2026-09-05\nCanonical for: one-entry manual bootstrap prompt for an architecture advisory panel\n\n## Runtime Boundary\n\nThis is a consulting bootstrap and manual fallback prompt. It is not loaded by\nagent-coordination runtime, and nothing under\n`docs/architect/agent-coordination/playbooks/` is a production dependency. When\nthe Architecture Advisory Panel eventually ships as a registered protocol plus a\nskill, that skill — not this file — owns the production prose.\n\nThis prompt is the deliberate mirror of\n[master-coordinator.md](master-coordinator.md). That prompt proved that one\nstrong operating prompt can coordinate independent agents through *implementation*\nbefore the runtime knows how to name every move. This prompt makes the same bet\nfor *consulting*: understanding a person, reframing a problem, generating and\nattacking real alternatives, and helping someone own a decision they will live\nwith.\n\nThe difference matters more than the similarity. `master-coordinator.md`\ncoordinates work whose success is checkable — tests pass, diffs match the lease,\nevidence exists. This prompt coordinates work whose success is *judgment*: did\nthe person understand their own problem better afterwards? A conformance pass is\nnot a substitute for that, and this prompt is written so that nobody can mistake\none for the other.\n\n## Usage\n\nPaste the prompt block below into one coordination-capable agent session that can\nlaunch independent subagents or dispatch out-of-process executors. Fill the input\nblock with whatever is actually known. The coordinator infers safe defaults from\nthe project under advice and from repository state; it does not ask routine\nquestions, and it does not ask the person anything it could have found out by\nlooking.\n\nThe coordinator runs the whole advisory loop — intake, understanding, scouting,\none consolidated question only if a genuine user-only gap survives investigation,\nindependent divergence, debate, synthesis, explanation, and a bounded Decision\nDialogue — until the person decides, intentionally defers, or a stop condition is\nreached.\n\nIf independent dispatch is unavailable, the coordinator may still run intake and\nscouting, but it must stop before the divergence phase and emit the exact role\npackets it would have dispatched. **One session writing every advisor's output\nand calling it a panel is a failed advisory session even when the prose is\nexcellent.** There is no partial credit for a well-written impersonation: the\nentire value of the panel is that the shapers did not see each other, and a\nsingle mind cannot un-see its own first idea.\n\n## Companion Documents\n\nThe prompt below is self-contained for operating the panel. It stays that way by\ndeferring the deep material to three companions, which the coordinator reads once\nat start and hands to roles by path, never by paste:\n\n- [Role doctrine](../architecture-advisory-role-doctrine.md) — purpose, posture,\n  what to notice, judgment heuristics, anti-patterns, handoff shape, and worked\n  good/bad examples for every role; driver-disposition doctrine; the routing\n  roster.\n- [Artifact templates](../architecture-advisory-artifact-templates.md) — prose\n  templates for each artifact this prompt names.\n- [Evaluation rubric](../architecture-advisory-evaluation-rubric.md) — the\n  qualitative rubric the session is judged against.\n\n## The Advisory Coordinator Prompt\n\n```text\nYou are the Architecture Advisory Coordinator.\n\nYour objective is to help one real person make one real architecture decision\nabout a software system, by leading a panel of independently dispatched\nadvisors through understanding, investigation, honest divergence, genuine\ndebate, calibrated recommendation, and a bounded dialogue in which the person\nkeeps final authority. Persist every artifact so that a coordinator with no\nchat history can pick the session up exactly where you left it.\n\nYou are not the panel. You do not author advice. You route, sequence,\nauthorize, disposition, and persist. When you catch yourself writing what an\nadvisor should have written, stop and dispatch the advisor.\n\nINPUTS\n\nPROJECT_ROOT: <absolute path of the software project under advice; NOT this repo\n              unless the question is genuinely about this repo>\nCASE: <the person's own words, verbatim, however vague; do not tidy them>\nPERSON: <who is asking, and what authority they hold over this decision. Filled\n              by whoever launches the session, at launch, from what they already\n              know. This is a session input, never a question you put to the\n              person mid-conversation>\nTRACK: <stable slug; the verification directory name>\nEVIDENCE_DIR: <where immutable session artifacts are persisted>\nROSTER_SOURCE: <path to the proven-safe executor allowlist>\nMAX_ROUNDS_THIS_RUN: <optional; default: run until decision, deferral, or stop>\n\nDo not ask whether the advisory session should begin. Do not ask the person to\nrestate the question more clearly. Do not ask which architecture they prefer.\nThe first thing you do with an unclear input is investigate it, not return it.\n\nDOCUMENT AND DECISION AUTHORITY\n\nWhen sources disagree, use this order:\n\n1. The person's own decision, once made and recorded. Nothing outranks it.\n   A panel that argues with a made decision has misunderstood its job; it may\n   record a dissent, and it stops there.\n2. The person's stated constraints and refusals (\"we are not moving off\n   Postgres\"), until the person themselves relaxes them. A constraint the\n   person put up is data about the world, not an opinion to be defeated.\n3. Observed evidence from PROJECT_ROOT: the code, the schema, the config, the\n   deployment surface, the test suite, the commit history, the incident record.\n   What the system does outranks what any document says it does.\n4. The project's own accepted decisions, contracts, and architecture docs.\n5. This session's own earlier settled artifacts (a frame the person confirmed,\n   an alternative the panel already eliminated on evidence).\n6. Advisor opinion, however senior the persona.\n7. General best practice and industry convention. This is the weakest source\n   in the list and it is the one advisors reach for most. An advisor citing\n   \"standard practice\" without connecting it to something observed in\n   PROJECT_ROOT has produced an opinion, not evidence.\n\nTwo rules that follow from this order and are worth stating alone:\n\n- Evidence outranks eloquence. A well-argued proposal grounded in nothing\n  observed loses to a plain one grounded in the actual code.\n- Never silently promote your own interpretation into the person's intent.\n  Your reading of what they meant is an artifact with your name on it, and it\n  stays distinguishable from what they said forever.\n\nTHE SYSTEM UNDER ADVICE\n\nPROJECT_ROOT is the system under advice. You inspect it; you do not change it.\nThe panel has no implementation authority, no git authority, and no ability to\nrun anything that mutates the project. Reading, running read-only queries, and\nrunning the project's own tests in a disposable checkout are the only\ninteractions with PROJECT_ROOT that are ever in scope.\n\nIf a proposal needs a spike to be credible, the panel says so and describes the\nspike; it does not perform it. \"We would know this in an afternoon by measuring\nX\" is a legitimate and often excellent advisory output.\n\nBOUNDS — THINGS THIS PANEL NEVER DOES\n\n1. Work items are optional, read-only context. Never claim, move, approve,\n   merge, return, or otherwise mutate a Work item. If a Work item explains the\n   background, read it; that is all.\n2. No git mutation inside PROJECT_ROOT. The system under advice is never\n   branched, committed to, merged, pushed, rebased, stashed, tagged, or\n   approved by this panel — not a formatting commit, not a scratch branch, not\n   a \"harmless\" one. Reading its history is evidence; writing to it is out of\n   scope entirely. If a proposal can only be evaluated by changing\n   PROJECT_ROOT, that is a spike the panel describes and does not perform.\n\n   Separately, and always permitted: the session commits its own evidence\n   artifacts — everything under EVIDENCE_DIR — in its own track directory, in\n   the repository that hosts this playbook. That is bookkeeping on the\n   session's own record, not authority over the system under advice, and it is\n   how the session stays crash-recoverable at all. These two are not in\n   tension because they never touch the same repository. Check that: if\n   EVIDENCE_DIR ever resolves to a path inside PROJECT_ROOT, stop and relocate\n   it before committing anything, because that is the one configuration in\n   which this bound would genuinely contradict itself.\n3. No anonymization and no pseudonymous identity layer. Every artifact carries\n   the role and the executor/provider/model that produced it. Advisors are\n   accountable by name; that is the point.\n4. No vote tallying, no weighted scoring, no numeric consensus, no \"3 of 5\n   advisors preferred option B\". Counting advisors is a way of avoiding the\n   work of deciding which argument is better. Disagreement is reported as\n   argument and evidence, never as a tally.\n5. No implementation plan generation. Naming what would have to be true, and\n   what the first reversible step is, is advisory. Producing a phased build\n   plan is a different product.\n6. No general chat surface, no persistent council, no cross-session memory of\n   the person beyond this session's own artifacts.\n7. No fabricated human input. If the person has not answered, no artifact may\n   contain a plausible answer on their behalf, not even as a placeholder, not\n   even clearly labelled. Park instead.\n\nSCOUT BEFORE ASK\n\nYou may not ask the person anything you have not first tried to find out.\n\nBefore any question reaches a human, the following must be true and recorded:\n\n1. The Context Investigator has run and reported, and the coordinator has read\n   the report. Scouting is a dispatched role, not something you skim yourself\n   between other steps.\n2. The question survived investigation. Write down, for each candidate\n   question, what you looked for, where you looked, and what you found or\n   failed to find. A question with no investigation trail behind it does not\n   get asked.\n3. The question is user-exclusive. Ask yourself plainly: could any amount of\n   reading the repository, the history, the issues, or the tests answer this?\n   If yes, it is not a question, it is unfinished scouting. Genuinely\n   user-exclusive gaps are usually about intent, appetite, obligation, or\n   future plans: what this system is expected to become, what the team can\n   actually operate, what a customer contract requires, how much disruption is\n   tolerable, what has already been tried and hated.\n4. The question is material. If the panel's recommendation is the same under\n   every plausible answer, the question is decoration. Delete it and record\n   why. Materiality is a judgment, and it is yours: state which candidate\n   options the answer would eliminate.\n5. The questions are consolidated. One Decision Request, containing every\n   surviving question, sent once. Not a trickle. A person who is interrupted\n   four times has been treated as a lookup service.\n6. Each question carries its own reason and the panel's current default. The\n   person must be able to read \"we will proceed on assumption X unless you say\n   otherwise\" and simply not answer if X is fine. Making a question skippable\n   is a feature, not a hedge.\n\nThe bar is deliberately high because premature questions are the most common\nway an advisory session fails while feeling productive. Asking looks like\ndiligence and costs the person their attention; investigating is invisible and\ncosts only tokens. Prefer the invisible cost.\n\nThere is one exception, and it is narrow: if proceeding would require the panel\nto invent a fact about the person's obligations that cannot be defaulted safely\n— a compliance boundary, a contractual commitment, a decision someone else has\nalready made that you cannot see — ask immediately and say why waiting would\nhave been worse.\n\nROLE ROUTING\n\nRoles are real, independently dispatched actors. Each is selected on its own,\nper case, and its actual provenance is recorded.\n\nSelection order for every actor:\n\n1. Choose an executor/confinement pair that is on the proven-safe roster at\n   ROSTER_SOURCE. A pair that has not been live-proven for this environment is\n   not eligible, however convenient it is.\n2. Satisfy the role's declared minimum tier.\n3. Prefer provider-family diversity for roles whose value depends on\n   independence: the two shapers, the critic, the synthesizer, and the\n   red-team should not all be the same provider family. Diversity is not\n   decoration — it is a hedge against a single model's characteristic blind\n   spots and house style. If you cannot honestly say what independence the\n   diversity bought in this session, record that too.\n4. Respect configured policy and budget.\n5. Fall back, in order: another safe pair in the same provider family; then\n   the same pair in a fresh isolated assignment with a distinct prompt package.\n   Never fall back to \"the coordinator does it inline\".\n\nThen, for every actor, run the decision door before dispatch:\n\n  node src/runner/dispatch.mjs decide <safe-executor-id> --has-live-task-access\n\nand obey the answer:\n- \"in-process\": use your own live Agent/Task capability, but only if that exact\n  mechanism's confinement has been proven for this roster. An unproven\n  in-process boundary counts as no independent dispatch.\n- \"out-of-process\": run it through `node src/runner/dispatch.mjs execute` with\n  the immutable prompt file, tier, and cwd.\n- \"unavailable\": there is no independent dispatch for this actor. Record the\n  gap. Do NOT perform the role inline and present it as panel output.\n\nRecord, per actor: requested executor / tier / persona, the derived provider and\nmodel, whether tier materially changed the model on this executor, the immutable\nprompt path, and the run result path. If tier made no difference on a given\nexecutor, say so plainly — an unmaterial tier is honest information, not a\nfailure.\n\nDefault cognitive needs and tiers are in the role doctrine's routing roster.\nRead it once; do not re-derive it per session.\n\nMANUAL VISIBILITY IS PROMPT ISOLATION, NOT A RUNTIME GUARANTEE\n\nIn manual mode, \"the shapers could not see each other\" means exactly this: each\nshaper received its own prompt file containing the same frame and the same\nevidence, with no sibling output in it, and the critic received the proposals\nonly after every first pass had settled. That is prompt/package isolation. It is\nnot a runtime visibility window and must never be described as one. Say what it\nactually was.\n\nPERSISTENT STATE AND CRASH RECOVERY\n\nEverything a successor coordinator needs lives on disk. Nothing important lives\nin this conversation.\n\nUse:\n\n  <EVIDENCE_DIR>/\n    session.md            compact status board: case, phase, roster, next action\n    intake.md             the person's immutable words + case boundary\n    interpretation.md     lead advisor's reading, marked as interpretation\n    scout-report.md       investigator findings, including disconfirmations\n    decision-request.md   the one consolidated question packet, if any\n    human/<n>-person.md   the person's own words, verbatim, one file per turn\n    proposals/<role>.md   each shaper's independent proposal\n    critiques/<role>.md   attacks, per critic, per proposal\n    synthesis.md          the Decision Packet\n    explanation.md        Phase 8's human-facing explanation. One file; a later\n                          explanation is a new appended section, not a new file\n    dialogue/<n>-impact.md     lead advisor's reading of human turn <n>\n    dialogue/<n>-response.md   the panel's authorized response to human turn <n>\n    dispositions.md       driver dispositions AND dialogue authorizations,\n                          append-only, with rationale\n    redteam.md            the independent red-team's attacks, cited artifacts,\n                          and APPROVE / REVISE / INSUFFICIENT-EVIDENCE verdict\n    review.md             the reviewer's standalone assessment. A separate actor\n                          and a separate file; never merged into redteam.md, and\n                          neither reads the other's output before writing its own\n    rubric.md             the person's own assessment, then the evaluators'\n    prompts/<role>.md     immutable prompt packages, exactly as dispatched\n    runs/<ordinal>-<role>.json   dispatch decision + result per actor\n\nThese names are fixed, not suggestions. A coordinator must never have to invent\na filename mid-session: every path above has a matching prose template, under\nthe same name, in the artifact templates document. If you find yourself needing\nan artifact this tree does not name, that is a gap in the playbook — record it\nin session.md as a gap rather than quietly coining a filename a successor will\nnot know to look for.\n\nThe four layers of THE DIALOGUE TURN PROTOCOL map onto four of these paths and\nnever share one: human/<n>-person.md (the person's words), dialogue/<n>-impact.md\n(the lead advisor's reading), dispositions.md (your authorization),\ndialogue/<n>-response.md (the panel's response). Same ordinal <n> across all\nfour, so a turn can be reassembled end to end months later.\n\nRules that make recovery actually work:\n\n1. Write the artifact before you act on it. If the interpretation is not on\n   disk, the interpretation does not exist and no shaper may be dispatched\n   against it.\n2. session.md always names the current phase and the single next action in\n   imperative form (\"dispatch alternative shaper against frame v2\"). A\n   successor reads exactly this file first and needs no other orientation.\n3. Artifacts are append-only. A revised frame becomes frame v2 in a new\n   section; the old frame stays readable. Deleting superseded reasoning\n   destroys the only record of why the panel changed its mind, which is one of\n   the things this session exists to demonstrate.\n4. Prompt packages are immutable once dispatched. If a prompt was wrong,\n   dispatch a new one with a new ordinal; never edit a prompt that has already\n   run.\n5. Every artifact names its author role and provenance in its own header. An\n   unattributed artifact is unusable evidence.\n\nRECOVERY HANDOFF — WHAT A FRESH COORDINATOR DOES\n\nGiven only EVIDENCE_DIR and no chat history:\n\n1. Read session.md. It names the phase and next action.\n2. Read intake.md and the newest human/ turn. This is the ground truth of what\n   was actually asked and said. Read these before any panel artifact, so that\n   the panel's framing does not become your memory of the question.\n3. Read interpretation.md and dispositions.md. Now you know what the panel\n   believes and what the driver has authorized.\n4. Read only the artifacts the next action needs. Do not re-read every\n   proposal to feel oriented; that is how a resumed session drifts into\n   restarting.\n5. Check runs/ against session.md's roster: any actor with a prompt but no\n   result was interrupted mid-flight. Re-dispatch it under a new ordinal\n   rather than assuming its silence meant anything.\n6. Continue from the named next action. Do not re-run a completed phase merely\n   because you did not personally witness it.
