This\n  supersedes the original v1 \"does not exist yet, Deferred Idea\" wording\n  — `tsk-2qz` reverses that decision deliberately, per\n  `docs/distribution-vision.md` §3's trụ cột 3.\n- **RUL12 (setup also runs every registered fix, unconditionally).** Legacy `fgos setup` also runs every registered fix (the same\n  `runFixes()` `doctor --fix` calls per RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix)), unconditionally and with no\n  confirmation — consistent with RUL10 (setup never asks for confirmation, acts then reports)'s own act-then-report contract for\n  this deprecated compatibility verb, not an exception to it. `setup`'s result gains a `fixed` array,\n  the same per-entry `{id, changed, message}` shape RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix) already describes\n  for `doctor --fix`'s own (per `tsk-5hi`,\n  `docs/history/setup-runs-registered-fixes/CONTEXT.md`).\n\n- **RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder; fgOS reads it first and never writes it; specified 2026-10-07; the lookup, the same-tier rule and the doctor check are built (runner decision 0057), the `fgctl init` skeleton and README are not).** A customer project that wants its own agent definitions (persona, role, decision boundary) puts them in `fgos/agents/<name>.yaml` at its project root. It is not `.fgos/`: that folder is runner state, ignored by git (`/.fgos/*`), every merge that stages a change under it is refused (`fgos-write-rejected`), and a fresh worktree has it stripped (ADR0020 (the runner strips .fgos/ from every fresh worktree)). It is not `.agents/` either: that is generated skill output which `fgos setup` and `npm run build:skills` rewrite. The first scope is `agents/` only; `workflows/`, `task-specs/` and `skills/` follow the same layout when a customer needs them, not before.\n  - Lookup, by name, first match wins: the workspace folder, then a domain or extension (`domains/<name>/agents/`), then the installed `core/agents`. A higher tier replaces the whole file of a lower one; fields are never merged. Two definitions of one name in the same tier are an error that `fgos doctor` reports, never a silent pick. This replaces the earlier rule that a name is unique across `core/agents` and every domain: a name is unique within a tier and a higher tier shadows a lower one.\n  - fgOS creates the folder and a README once, at onboarding (`fgctl init`), and never edits it afterwards; an fgOS upgrade never touches it. The installed tier is located through the release manifest, never through the working directory or PATH.\n  - Built: `src/runner/agent-definitions.mjs` is the one lookup (workspace, then `domains/*/agents/`, then `core/agents/`; a project without its own `domains/` or `core/agents/` folder reads the running package's). `fgos workflow start --seats \"@name|...\"` uses it and pins the text at start. The doctor check `agent-type-names-unique` now means unique within each tier, covers `fgos/agents`, and reports which definition each customization replaces. The unit-level and capability-level `persona:` names still read `core/agents` of the working project at dispatch.\n  - A doctor check registers with the feature and reports each customization, which installed definition it shadows, whether it has the shape the loader needs, and a shadowed core name or an override that no longer fits the installed set after an upgrade.\n  - Not customizable here: executor, model and provider policy (`config.json`) and the platform laws. An extension is treated as a domain until an extension loader exists.\n  - No component-boundary change: it extends the three-tier discovery convention coordination protocols already use (project, `domains/<name>/`, packaged `core/`) to agent definitions.\n\n- **RUL14 (the lazy-probe unlock rule: moved).** The rule that unlocks an account locked for a dead login with one real call now lives with the provider-capacity rules in `docs/specs/runner.md` (RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds)), together with the refresh-ahead and write-back rules for a rotating login (RUL75 (a rotating provider login is renewed once at the source, in a copy fgOS holds, and a login renewed inside a private home is written back)). This document keeps only where the state lives (row 5d).\n- **RUL15 (`fgctl init` needs no hand-downloaded tarball: it picks its release by a fixed precedence and downloads it checksum-verified; 2026-10-12).** The release `fgctl init` installs comes from the first of these that is set:\n  1. `--from <path | URL>` on the command line;\n  2. the `FGCTL_FROM=<path | URL>` environment variable (same meaning as the flag, for a non-release build: a `.tar.gz`, a release directory, or a URL);\n  3. `FGCTL_VERSION=<tag>`, which downloads exactly that tag's asset (needed for a pre-release, which \"latest\" never selects);\n  4. the release pinned by the project's committed `.fgos/distribution.json` (no network when that release is staged on the machine; otherwise see \"The pin records the tag\" below);\n  5. otherwise the latest GitHub release, found by following `<repo>/releases/latest` to its tag.\n  - An explicit source (1-3) beats a pin; the pin then only validates what was fetched (a different digest is refused as a pin mismatch, as for `--from` today). The inputs are read per invocation; nothing is remembered.\n  - **The pin records the tag.** When `fgctl init` installs from a download (latest or `FGCTL_VERSION`) and writes a new `.fgos/distribution.json`, it stores the resolved tag in `projectRuntime.releaseVersion` next to the digest (a local or URL source writes a digest-only pin with a null `releaseVersion`, never the build's own manifest version, which is not a download name; an existing pin is never rewritten). A pin with a tag whose digest is not staged on this machine (a teammate's fresh clone, or a quarantined release) makes a plain `fgctl init` download that tag, checksum-verified; the pin's digest must equal what was fetched, else `pin-mismatch` and nothing is activated. A tag written without the leading `v` (a hand-edited pin, for example `0.2.0`) is read as `v0.2.0`, the form releases are tagged in; if the download still fails, the error names the pinned tag and points to `FGCTL_VERSION` and `FGCTL_FROM` instead of surfacing a bare HTTP error. A digest-only pin (no tag) keeps the old behavior: it needs `--from`, `FGCTL_FROM` or `FGCTL_VERSION` on a machine that has not staged it. `fgctl upgrade` writes no tag (it takes a local path), so an upgraded pin goes back to digest-only unless the manifest carries its own version.\n  - A download fetches `fgos-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS` through the system `curl` with the same flags, timeouts and `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` override as `install.sh`; there is no HTTP/TLS library in `fgctl`. The target is detected the way the installers do (`FGCTL_TARGET` overrides; `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` are supported, see RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)) and an unsupported target refuses before any request.\n  - Verification is mandatory: the asset's own entry in `SHA256SUMS` (file name matched exactly) must equal the downloaded file's SHA-256, otherwise `fgctl init` refuses and writes nothing (no staging, no pin, no activation). A URL source must have `SHA256SUMS` in the same directory; a local path is trusted as given. The download lives in a private scratch directory under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fgos-work/` that is removed when init returns, success or not.\n  - The project must be inside a git repository, checked before any request is made (unchanged). `fgctl upgrade` and `fgctl stage` still take only `--from <path>`; they do not download.\n  - `curl` is an assumed tool (on Windows, the `curl.exe` that ships with Windows 10 and later): the `curl-available` doctor check reports it.\n- **RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell; 2026-10-13).** fgOS runs from a plain PowerShell or `cmd.exe` session on Windows 10 and later, with no Git Bash and no WSL.\n  - **Assets.** A release publishes, per target, `fgos-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` and `fgctl-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, one `SHA256SUMS` covering every asset, and both installers (`install.sh`, and `install.ps1`, which lives at `scripts/install.ps1` in the repository because the root-file allowlist is closed and is published under the name `install.ps1`). `tar.gz` is the one archive format on every target: Windows 10 and later ship `tar.exe` and `curl.exe`, and the Rust extractor already reads it. The Windows `fgos` tree carries the host as `bin/fgos.exe` (and `bin/fgos`, the manifest's entry name), a `bin/fgos-runner.cmd` beside the `sh` form of `bin/fgos-runner`, and declares `target: {os: windows, arch: x64}`. The Linux asset is built on `ubuntu-22.04`, and the build fails when a shipped binary needs a glibc symbol newer than `GLIBC_2.35` (`scripts/check-glibc-ceiling.sh`), so a binary never prints a loader error on the oldest supported distribution. A new platform is one row in `src/util/release-targets.mjs`, one in the Rust `host_target` table, one in each installer and one release-workflow matrix entry; macOS is not published.\n  - **`install.ps1`.** Same contract as `install.sh`: `FGCTL_VERSION`, `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR` (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\fgos\\bin`), `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` (http, https or `file://`), `FGCTL_TARGET`; the tarball's own `SHA256SUMS` entry must match or nothing is installed; a symlinked `fgctl.exe` is refused; every request is bounded by a timeout. It needs no administrator rights (an elevated session is refused unless `FGCTL_ALLOW_ROOT=1`, as `install.sh` refuses root), never changes `PATH`, and prints the commands that do. Like `install.sh`, with no `FGCTL_VERSION` it installs the latest NON-prerelease, so a pre-release needs `FGCTL_VERSION`.\n  - **Workspace launchers.** `fgctl init` and `fgctl repair` write four launchers into `.fgos/installation/bin/`: the `sh` pair `fgos`, `fgos-runner` (Linux, macOS, Git Bash) and the batch pair `fgos.cmd`, `fgos-runner.cmd` (PowerShell, `cmd.exe`; no `sh` involved). Each reads `activation.json`, refuses with exit 3 unless `status` is `ready`, and runs the active release's entry. A directory on `PATH` holding them makes `fgos` resolve in PowerShell through `PATHEXT`. The post-activation tail (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `doctor`) runs the `.cmd` form on a Windows host. `fgctl verify` checks that the launchers its host needs (the `sh` pair everywhere, the batch pair too on Windows) exist and equal what this `fgctl` writes; a missing or edited one is reported with `run fgctl repair` and never quarantines the (intact) release.\n  - **Proof.** Pushing a release tag builds both targets and runs a consumer proof on each, and only when both pass does the publish job run; publishing exists only in `release.yml`. The Windows proof (`scripts/ci-external-consumer.ps1`, under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7) installs `fgctl` with `install.ps1`, runs `fgctl init` against a local release server, runs the activated `fgos` from PowerShell and from `cmd.exe`, and checks that a tampered download is refused by both the installer and `fgctl init`.\n  - **Not covered.** Windows ARM64 and macOS have no asset. Outside a project it exits 127 and says to run `fgctl init`.\n  - The launcher carries a marker line.     "sectionText": "#### Business Rules\n\n- **RUL1 (distributed package never includes the source repo's own runtime data).** The distributed package never includes the source repository's own\n  runtime data directory or its own dogfood runner configuration — install\n  content is always limited to the distribution file allowlist.\n- **RUL2 (distribution is a GitHub install, not an npm registry publish).** Distribution happens by installing directly from the GitHub\n  repository, not by publishing to the public npm registry — no package\n  rename and no registry publish credentials are involved.\n- **RUL3 (install never changes init/doctrine/marker-detection behavior).** Installing fgos does not change init/doctrine/marker-detection\n  behavior in any way — that behavior belongs entirely to the coexistence\n  area and is unchanged by installation.\n- **RUL4 (every README Documentation link resolves to a shipped file).** Every link in the README's Documentation section resolves to a\n  file that is actually present in the distribution file allowlist — a link\n  to content that isn't shipped is a defect, not an acceptable pointer to\n  \"clone the repo for more\" (per str77-79-doc-gap-fixes / ea8b9a8d).\n  Contributor/maintainer-only documentation (decision records, area specs,\n  the product backlog, platform foundations) is intentionally excluded from\n  both the allowlist and that section — it is out of scope for an installed\n  end user, not an oversight.\n- **RUL5 (dev checkout shell helper is never sourced automatically).** The dev checkout shell helper file is never sourced automatically\n  by any install step or other mechanism in this repository — a contributor\n  adding it to their own shell profile is always their own explicit,\n  separate action.\n- **RUL6 (install never runs a lifecycle script).** Installing (from any of npm, pnpm, or yarn) never runs a lifecycle\n  script of its own — the contributor hooks setup is always a separate,\n  manually-invoked command, never an automatic `prepare`/`postinstall` step\n  (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle). This is what lets every package\n  manager's own build-script approval policy stay out of the way entirely,\n  rather than needing to be satisfied.\n- **RUL7 (setup/doctor cover both bash and zsh).** `fgos setup` and `fgos doctor` both cover bash and zsh — neither\n  shell is treated as a lesser case.\n- **RUL8 (setup's config update never overwrites a customized setting).** `fgos setup`'s config update never overwrites a setting the\n  caller already customized, at any nesting depth; array-valued settings\n  are never partially merged, only added wholesale when entirely missing.\n- **RUL9 (doctor's default path never writes anything).** `fgos doctor`'s default (no `--fix`) path never writes\n  anything, under any circumstance, including when a check would\n  otherwise need to create a file to check it — a missing config file is\n  reported as missing, never created as a side effect of checking.\n  `--fix` is the deliberate exception: it runs every registered fix\n  (Data Dictionary #7b) before re-reporting checks — reversed from the\n  original no-exceptions wording per `tsk-2qz`, which reverses this\n  rule and RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix) together (`docs/history/doctor-fix-gate-bypass/\n  CONTEXT.md`).\n- **RUL10 (setup never asks for confirmation, acts then reports).** `fgos setup` never asks for confirmation before writing to a\n  shell profile or the config file — it acts and then reports exactly what\n  it changed. ## Business Rules

- **RUL1 (distributed package never includes the source repo's own runtime data).** The distributed package never includes the source repository's own
  runtime data directory or its own dogfood runner configuration — install
  content is always limited to the distribution file allowlist.
- **RUL2 (distribution is a GitHub install, not an npm registry publish).** Distribution happens by installing directly from the GitHub
  repository, not by publishing to the public npm registry — no package
  rename and no registry publish credentials are involved.
- **RUL3 (install never changes init/doctrine/marker-detection behavior).** Installing fgos does not change init/doctrine/marker-detection
  behavior in any way — that behavior belongs entirely to the coexistence
  area and is unchanged by installation.
- **RUL4 (every README Documentation link resolves to a shipped file).** Every link in the README's Documentation section resolves to a
  file that is actually present in the distribution file allowlist — a link
  to content that isn't shipped is a defect, not an acceptable pointer to
  "clone the repo for more" (per str77-79-doc-gap-fixes / ea8b9a8d).
  Contributor/maintainer-only documentation (decision records, area specs,
  the product backlog, platform foundations) is intentionally excluded from
  both the allowlist and that section — it is out of scope for an installed
  end user, not an oversight.
- **RUL5 (dev checkout shell helper is never sourced automatically).** The dev checkout shell helper file is never sourced automatically
  by any install step or other mechanism in this repository — a contributor
  adding it to their own shell profile is always their own explicit,
  separate action.
- **RUL6 (install never runs a lifecycle script).** Installing (from any of npm, pnpm, or yarn) never runs a lifecycle
  script of its own — the contributor hooks setup is always a separate,
  manually-invoked command, never an automatic `prepare`/`postinstall` step
  (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle). This is what lets every package
  manager's own build-script approval policy stay out of the way entirely,
  rather than needing to be satisfied.
- **RUL7 (setup/doctor cover both bash and zsh).** `fgos setup` and `fgos doctor` both cover bash and zsh — neither
  shell is treated as a lesser case.
- **RUL8 (setup's config update never overwrites a customized setting).** `fgos setup`'s config update never overwrites a setting the
  caller already customized, at any nesting depth; array-valued settings
  are never partially merged, only added wholesale when entirely missing.
- **RUL9 (doctor's default path never writes anything).** `fgos doctor`'s default (no `--fix`) path never writes
  anything, under any circumstance, including when a check would
  otherwise need to create a file to check it — a missing config file is
  reported as missing, never created as a side effect of checking.
  `--fix` is the deliberate exception: it runs every registered fix
  (Data Dictionary #7b) before re-reporting checks — reversed from the
  original no-exceptions wording per `tsk-2qz`, which reverses this
  rule and RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix) together (`docs/history/doctor-fix-gate-bypass/
  CONTEXT.md`).
- **RUL10 (setup never asks for confirmation, acts then reports).** `fgos setup` never asks for confirmation before writing to a
  shell profile or the config file — it acts and then reports exactly what
  it changed. Every other verb, and both of these two without
  `--pretty`, still produce the same enveloped-JSON result shape as before
  this feature — `--pretty` only changes how that same result is displayed,
  never what it contains.
- **RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix).** `fgos doctor --fix` exists and is real: it runs every fix
  registered via `registerFix` (Data Dictionary #7b) against the current
  cwd before re-reporting checks, then returns the same checks shape as
  the no-flag path plus a `fixed` array. The fix list is a registry, not
  a fixed set — a module can register a new one the same way a check or
  config-default is registered, independent of either (per tsk-2cs). This
  supersedes the original v1 "does not exist yet, Deferred Idea" wording
  — `tsk-2qz` reverses that decision deliberately, per
  `docs/distribution-vision.md` §3's trụ cột 3.
- **RUL12 (setup also runs every registered fix, unconditionally).** Legacy `fgos setup` also runs every registered fix (the same
  `runFixes()` `doctor --fix` calls per RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix)), unconditionally and with no
  confirmation — consistent with RUL10 (setup never asks for confirmation, acts then reports)'s own act-then-report contract for
  this deprecated compatibility verb, not an exception to it. `setup`'s result gains a `fixed` array,
  the same per-entry `{id, changed, message}` shape RUL11 (doctor --fix exists and is real, runs every registered fix) already describes
  for `doctor --fix`'s own (per `tsk-5hi`,
  `docs/history/setup-runs-registered-fixes/CONTEXT.md`).

- **RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder; fgOS reads it first and never writes it; specified 2026-10-07; the lookup, the same-tier rule and the doctor check are built (runner decision 0057), the `fgctl init` skeleton and README are not).** A customer project that wants its own agent definitions (persona, role, decision boundary) puts them in `fgos/agents/<name>.yaml` at its project root. It is not `.fgos/`: that folder is runner state, ignored by git (`/.fgos/*`), every merge that stages a change under it is refused (`fgos-write-rejected`), and a fresh worktree has it stripped (ADR0020 (the runner strips .fgos/ from every fresh worktree)). It is not `.agents/` either: that is generated skill output which `fgos setup` and `npm run build:skills` rewrite. The first scope is `agents/` only; `workflows/`, `task-specs/` and `skills/` follow the same layout when a customer needs them, not before.
  - Lookup, by name, first match wins: the workspace folder, then a domain or extension (`domains/<name>/agents/`), then the installed `core/agents`. A higher tier replaces the whole file of a lower one; fields are never merged. Two definitions of one name in the same tier are an error that `fgos doctor` reports, never a silent pick. This replaces the earlier rule that a name is unique across `core/agents` and every domain: a name is unique within a tier and a higher tier shadows a lower one.
  - fgOS creates the folder and a README once, at onboarding (`fgctl init`), and never edits it afterwards; an fgOS upgrade never touches it. The installed tier is located through the release manifest, never through the working directory or PATH.
  - Built: `src/runner/agent-definitions.mjs` is the one lookup (workspace, then `domains/*/agents/`, then `core/agents/`; a project without its own `domains/` or `core/agents/` folder reads the running package's). `fgos workflow start --seats "@name|..."` uses it and pins the text at start. The doctor check `agent-type-names-unique` now means unique within each tier, covers `fgos/agents`, and reports which definition each customization replaces. The unit-level and capability-level `persona:` names still read `core/agents` of the working project at dispatch.
  - A doctor check registers with the feature and reports each customization, which installed definition it shadows, whether it has the shape the loader needs, and a shadowed core name or an override that no longer fits the installed set after an upgrade.
  - Not customizable here: executor, model and provider policy (`config.json`) and the platform laws. An extension is treated as a domain until an extension loader exists.
  - No component-boundary change: it extends the three-tier discovery convention coordination protocols already use (project, `domains/<name>/`, packaged `core/`) to agent definitions.

- **RUL14 (the lazy-probe unlock rule: moved).** The rule that unlocks an account locked for a dead login with one real call now lives with the provider-capacity rules in `docs/specs/runner.md` (RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds)), together with the refresh-ahead and write-back rules for a rotating login (RUL75 (a rotating provider login is renewed once at the source, in a copy fgOS holds, and a login renewed inside a private home is written back)). This document keeps only where the state lives (row 5d).
- **RUL15 (`fgctl init` needs no hand-downloaded tarball: it picks its release by a fixed precedence and downloads it checksum-verified; 2026-10-12).** The release `fgctl init` installs comes from the first of these that is set:
  1. `--from <path | URL>` on the command line;
  2. the `FGCTL_FROM=<path | URL>` environment variable (same meaning as the flag, for a non-release build: a `.tar.gz`, a release directory, or a URL);
  3. `FGCTL_VERSION=<tag>`, which downloads exactly that tag's asset (needed for a pre-release, which "latest" never selects);
  4. the release pinned by the project's committed `.fgos/distribution.json` (no network when that release is staged on the machine; otherwise see "The pin records the tag" below);
  5. otherwise the latest GitHub release, found by following `<repo>/releases/latest` to its tag.
  - An explicit source (1-3) beats a pin; the pin then only validates what was fetched (a different digest is refused as a pin mismatch, as for `--from` today). The inputs are read per invocation; nothing is remembered.
  - **The pin records the tag.** When `fgctl init` or `fgctl upgrade` installs from a download (latest or `FGCTL_VERSION`) and writes `.fgos/distribution.json`, it stores the resolved tag in `projectRuntime.releaseVersion` next to the digest (a local or URL source writes a digest-only pin with a null `releaseVersion`, never the build's own manifest version, which is not a download name; `init` never rewrites an existing pin, while `upgrade` rewrites the pin to the upgraded release). A pin with a tag whose digest is not staged on this machine (a teammate's fresh clone, or a quarantined release) makes a plain `fgctl init` download that tag, checksum-verified; the pin's digest must equal what was fetched, else `pin-mismatch` and nothing is activated. A tag written without the leading `v` (a hand-edited pin, for example `0.2.0`) is read as `v0.2.0`, the form releases are tagged in; if the download still fails, the error names the pinned tag and points to `FGCTL_VERSION` and `FGCTL_FROM` instead of surfacing a bare HTTP error. A digest-only pin (no tag) keeps the old behavior: it needs `--from`, `FGCTL_FROM` or `FGCTL_VERSION` on a machine that has not staged it.
  - A download fetches `fgos-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS` through the system `curl` with the same flags, timeouts and `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` override as `install.sh`; there is no HTTP/TLS library in `fgctl`. The target is detected the way the installers do (`FGCTL_TARGET` overrides; `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` are supported, see RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)) and an unsupported target refuses before any request.
  - Verification is mandatory: the asset's own entry in `SHA256SUMS` (file name matched exactly) must equal the downloaded file's SHA-256, otherwise `fgctl init` / `fgctl upgrade` refuses and writes nothing (no staging, no pin, no activation). A URL source must have `SHA256SUMS` in the same directory; a local path is trusted as given. The download lives in a private scratch directory under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fgos-work/` that is removed when the command returns, success or not.
  - The project must be inside a git repository, checked before any request is made (unchanged). `fgctl upgrade` resolves its candidate by `--from <path | URL>` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > the latest GitHub release (it ignores the current pin so a plain `fgctl upgrade` moves to the latest release). `fgctl stage` still takes only `--from <path>`; it does not download.
  - `curl` is an assumed tool (on Windows, the `curl.exe` that ships with Windows 10 and later): the `curl-available` doctor check reports it.
- **RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell; 2026-10-13).** fgOS runs from a plain PowerShell or `cmd.exe` session on Windows 10 and later, with no Git Bash and no WSL.
  - **Assets.** A release publishes, per target, `fgos-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` and `fgctl-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, one `SHA256SUMS` covering every asset, and both installers (`install.sh`, and `install.ps1`, which lives at `scripts/install.ps1` in the repository because the root-file allowlist is closed and is published under the name `install.ps1`). `tar.gz` is the one archive format on every target: Windows 10 and later ship `tar.exe` and `curl.exe`, and the Rust extractor already reads it. The Windows `fgos` tree carries the host as `bin/fgos.exe` (and `bin/fgos`, the manifest's entry name), a `bin/fgos-runner.cmd` beside the `sh` form of `bin/fgos-runner`, and declares `target: {os: windows, arch: x64}`. The Linux asset is built on `ubuntu-22.04`, and the build fails when a shipped binary needs a glibc symbol newer than `GLIBC_2.35` (`scripts/check-glibc-ceiling.sh`), so a binary never prints a loader error on the oldest supported distribution. A new platform is one row in `src/util/release-targets.mjs`, one in the Rust `host_target` table, one in each installer and one release-workflow matrix entry; macOS is not published.
  - **`install.ps1`.** Same contract as `install.sh`: `FGCTL_VERSION`, `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR` (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\fgos\bin`), `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` (http, https or `file://`), `FGCTL_TARGET`; the tarball's own `SHA256SUMS` entry must match or nothing is installed; a symlinked `fgctl.exe` is refused; every request is bounded by a timeout. It needs no administrator rights (an elevated session is refused unless `FGCTL_ALLOW_ROOT=1`, as `install.sh` refuses root), never changes `PATH`, and prints the commands that do. Like `install.sh`, with no `FGCTL_VERSION` it installs the latest NON-prerelease, so a pre-release needs `FGCTL_VERSION`.
  - **Workspace launchers.** `fgctl init` and `fgctl repair` write four launchers into `.fgos/installation/bin/`: the `sh` pair `fgos`, `fgos-runner` (Linux, macOS, Git Bash) and the batch pair `fgos.cmd`, `fgos-runner.cmd` (PowerShell, `cmd.exe`; no `sh` involved). A directory on `PATH` holding them makes `fgos` resolve in PowerShell through `PATHEXT`. - **RUL14 (the lazy-probe unlock rule: moved).** The rule that unlocks an account locked for a dead login with one real call now lives with the provider-capacity rules in `docs/specs/runner.md` (RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds)), together with the refresh-ahead and write-back rules for a rotating login (RUL75 (a rotating provider login is renewed once at the source, in a copy fgOS holds, and a login renewed inside a private home is written back)). This document keeps only where the state lives (row 5d).
- **RUL15 (`fgctl init` needs no hand-downloaded tarball: it picks its release by a fixed precedence and downloads it checksum-verified; 2026-10-12).** The release `fgctl init` installs comes from the first of these that is set:
  1. `--from <path | URL>` on the command line;
  2. the `FGCTL_FROM=<path | URL>` environment variable (same meaning as the flag, for a non-release build: a `.tar.gz`, a release directory, or a URL);
  3. `FGCTL_VERSION=<tag>`, which downloads exactly that tag's asset (needed for a pre-release, which "latest" never selects);
  4. the release pinned by the project's committed `.fgos/distribution.json` (no network when that release is staged on the machine; otherwise see "The pin records the tag" below);
  5. otherwise the latest GitHub release, found by following `<repo>/releases/latest` to its tag.
  - An explicit source (1-3) beats a pin; the pin then only validates what was fetched (a different digest is refused as a pin mismatch, as for `--from` today). The inputs are read per invocation; nothing is remembered.
  - **The pin records the tag.** When `fgctl init` installs from a download (latest or `FGCTL_VERSION`) and writes a new `.fgos/distribution.json`, it stores the resolved tag in `projectRuntime.releaseVersion` next to the digest (a local or URL source writes a digest-only pin with a null `releaseVersion`, never the build's own manifest version, which is not a download name; an existing pin is never rewritten). A pin with a tag whose digest is not staged on this machine (a teammate's fresh clone, or a quarantined release) makes a plain `fgctl init` download that tag, checksum-verified; the pin's digest must equal what was fetched, else `pin-mismatch` and nothing is activated. A tag written without the leading `v` (a hand-edited pin, for example `0.2.0`) is read as `v0.2.0`, the form releases are tagged in; if the download still fails, the error names the pinned tag and points to `FGCTL_VERSION` and `FGCTL_FROM` instead of surfacing a bare HTTP error. A digest-only pin (no tag) keeps the old behavior: it needs `--from`, `FGCTL_FROM` or `FGCTL_VERSION` on a machine that has not staged it. `fgctl upgrade` writes no tag (it takes a local path), so an upgraded pin goes back to digest-only unless the manifest carries its own version.
  - A download fetches `fgos-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS` through the system `curl` with the same flags, timeouts and `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` override as `install.sh`; there is no HTTP/TLS library in `fgctl`. The target is detected the way the installers do (`FGCTL_TARGET` overrides; `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` are supported, see RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)) and an unsupported target refuses before any request.
  - Verification is mandatory: the asset's own entry in `SHA256SUMS` (file name matched exactly) must equal the downloaded file's SHA-256, otherwise `fgctl init` refuses and writes nothing (no staging, no pin, no activation). A URL source must have `SHA256SUMS` in the same directory; a local path is trusted as given. The download lives in a private scratch directory under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fgos-work/` that is removed when init returns, success or not.
  - The project must be inside a git repository, checked before any request is made (unchanged). `fgctl upgrade` and `fgctl stage` still take only `--from <path>`; they do not download.
  - `curl` is an assumed tool (on Windows, the `curl.exe` that ships with Windows 10 and later): the `curl-available` doctor check reports it.
- **RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell; 2026-10-13).** fgOS runs from a plain PowerShell or `cmd.exe` session on Windows 10 and later, with no Git Bash and no WSL.
  - **Assets.** A release publishes, per target, `fgos-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` and `fgctl-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, one `SHA256SUMS` covering every asset, and both installers (`install.sh`, and `install.ps1`, which lives at `scripts/install.ps1` in the repository because the root-file allowlist is closed and is published under the name `install.ps1`). `tar.gz` is the one archive format on every target: Windows 10 and later ship `tar.exe` and `curl.exe`, and the Rust extractor already reads it. The Windows `fgos` tree carries the host as `bin/fgos.exe` (and `bin/fgos`, the manifest's entry name), a `bin/fgos-runner.cmd` beside the `sh` form of `bin/fgos-runner`, and declares `target: {os: windows, arch: x64}`. The Linux asset is built on `ubuntu-22.04`, and the build fails when a shipped binary needs a glibc symbol newer than `GLIBC_2.35` (`scripts/check-glibc-ceiling.sh`), so a binary never prints a loader error on the oldest supported distribution. A new platform is one row in `src/util/release-targets.mjs`, one in the Rust `host_target` table, one in each installer and one release-workflow matrix entry; macOS is not published.
  - **`install.ps1`.** Same contract as `install.sh`: `FGCTL_VERSION`, `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR` (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\fgos\bin`), `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` (http, https or `file://`), `FGCTL_TARGET`; the tarball's own `SHA256SUMS` entry must match or nothing is installed; a symlinked `fgctl.exe` is refused; every request is bounded by a timeout. It needs no administrator rights (an elevated session is refused unless `FGCTL_ALLOW_ROOT=1`, as `install.sh` refuses root), never changes `PATH`, and prints the commands that do. Like `install.sh`, with no `FGCTL_VERSION` it installs the latest NON-prerelease, so a pre-release needs `FGCTL_VERSION`.
  - **Workspace launchers.** `fgctl init` and `fgctl repair` write four launchers into `.fgos/installation/bin/`: the `sh` pair `fgos`, `fgos-runner` (Linux, macOS, Git Bash) and the batch pair `fgos.cmd`, `fgos-runner.cmd` (PowerShell, `cmd.exe`; no `sh` involved). Each reads `activation.json`, refuses with exit 3 unless `status` is `ready`, and runs the active release's entry. A directory on `PATH` holding them makes `fgos` resolve in PowerShell through `PATHEXT`. The post-activation tail (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `doctor`) runs the `.cmd` form on a Windows host. `fgctl verify` checks that the launchers its host needs (the `sh` pair everywhere, the batch pair too on Windows) exist and equal what this `fgctl` writes; a missing or edited one is reported with `run fgctl repair` and never quarantines the (intact) release.
  - **Proof.** Pushing a release tag builds both targets and runs a consumer proof on each, and only when both pass does the publish job run; publishing exists only in `release.yml`. The Windows proof (`scripts/ci-external-consumer.ps1`, under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7) installs `fgctl` with `install.ps1`, runs `fgctl init` against a local release server, runs the activated `fgos` from PowerShell and from `cmd.exe`, and checks that a tampered download is refused by both the installer and `fgctl init`.
  - **Not covered.** Windows ARM64 and macOS have no asset. The machine release store stays at `%USERPROFILE%\.local\state\fgos` (`FGOS_STATE_HOME` moves it); relocating it to `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is a separate decision.
- **RUL17 (one `fgos` on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos; `doctor --fix` provides it; 2026-10-13).** A release install puts only `fgctl` on PATH and `fgctl init` activates a release per project, so a plain `fgos` used to need an absolute path. `fgos doctor` check `project-fgos-launcher` and its registered fix own the answer, and `fgctl init` already ends by running `doctor --fix`:
  - The fix writes one small launcher named `fgos` (`fgos.cmd` on Windows) into the directory `fgctl` was found in on `PATH`. The launcher walks up from the working directory to the nearest `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` and runs it with the same arguments, so each project runs the release it activated, from any subdirectory, in any shell, interactive or not; it edits no rc file. Outside a project it exits 127 and says to run `fgctl init`.
  - The launcher carries a marker line. The check reports `ready`, an out-of-date copy (rewritten by the fix), a foreign `fgos` found first on `PATH` (never overwritten; the check names it), no `fgos` with `fgctl` on `PATH` (the fix writes it), or neither on `PATH` (the check says to add the directory `fgctl` was installed into).
  - A source checkout keeps the sourced shell-integration script and needs no launcher; the check passes there.
  - Proof: `test/setup/project-launcher.test.mjs` (two projects and a nested one each run their own fgos; the `cmd` launcher runs on Windows in the focused Windows job).

Outside a project it exits 127 and says to run `fgctl init`.\n  - The launcher carries a marker line. The inputs are read per invocation; nothing is remembered.\n  - **The pin records the tag.** When `fgctl init` installs from a download (latest or `FGCTL_VERSION`) and writes a new `.fgos/distribution.json`, it stores the resolved tag in `projectRuntime.releaseVersion` next to the digest (a local or URL source writes a digest-only pin with a null `releaseVersion`, never the build's own manifest version, which is not a download name; an existing pin is never rewritten). A pin with a tag whose digest is not staged on this machine (a teammate's fresh clone, or a quarantined release) makes a plain `fgctl init` download that tag, checksum-verified; the pin's digest must equal what was fetched, else `pin-mismatch` and nothing is activated. A digest-only pin (no tag) keeps the old behavior: it needs `--from`, `FGCTL_FROM` or `FGCTL_VERSION` on a machine that has not staged it. `fgctl upgrade` writes no tag (it takes a local path), so an upgraded pin goes back to digest-only unless the manifest carries its own version.\n  - A download fetches `fgos-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS` through the system `curl` with the same flags, timeouts and `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` override as `install.sh`; there is no HTTP/TLS library in `fgctl`. - **RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell; 2026-10-13).** fgOS runs from a plain PowerShell or `cmd.exe` session on Windows 10 and later, with no Git Bash and no WSL.

The Windows `fgos` tree carries the host as `bin/fgos.exe` (and `bin/fgos`, the manifest's entry name), a `bin/fgos-runner.cmd` beside the `sh` form of `bin/fgos-runner`, and declares `target: {os: windows, arch: x64}`. The Linux asset is built on `ubuntu-22.04`, and the build fails when a shipped binary needs a glibc symbol newer than `GLIBC_2.35` (`scripts/check-glibc-ceiling.sh`), so a binary never prints a loader error on the oldest supported distribution. A new platform is one row in `src/util/release-targets.mjs`, one in the Rust `host_target` table, one in each installer and one release-workflow matrix entry; macOS is not published.
  - **`install.ps1`.** Same contract as `install.sh`: `FGCTL_VERSION`, `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR` (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\fgos\bin`), `FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL` (http, https or `file://`), `FGCTL_TARGET`; the tarball's own `SHA256SUMS` entry must match or nothing is installed; a symlinked `fgctl.exe` is refused; every request is bounded by a timeout. It needs no administrator rights (an elevated session is refused unless `FGCTL_ALLOW_ROOT=1`, as `install.sh` refuses root), never changes `PATH`, and prints the commands that do. Like `install.sh`, with no `FGCTL_VERSION` it installs the latest NON-prerelease, so a pre-release needs `FGCTL_VERSION`.
  - **Workspace launchers.** `fgctl init` and `fgctl repair` write four launchers into `.fgos/installation/bin/`: the `sh` pair `fgos`, `fgos-runner` (Linux, macOS, Git Bash) and the batch pair `fgos.cmd`, `fgos-runner.cmd` (PowerShell, `cmd.exe`; no `sh` involved). Each reads `activation.json`, refuses with exit 3 unless `status` is `ready`, and runs the active release's entry. A directory on `PATH` holding them makes `fgos` resolve in PowerShell through `PATHEXT`. The post-activation tail (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `doctor`) runs the `.cmd` form on a Windows host. `fgctl verify` checks that the launchers its host needs (the `sh` pair everywhere, the batch pair too on Windows) exist and equal what this `fgctl` writes; a missing or edited one is reported with `run fgctl repair` and never quarantines the (intact) release.
  - **Proof.** Pushing a release tag builds both targets and runs a consumer proof on each, and only when both pass does the publish job run; publishing exists only in `release.yml`. The Windows proof (`scripts/ci-external-consumer.ps1`, under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7) installs `fgctl` with `install.ps1`, runs `fgctl init` against a local release server, runs the activated `fgos` from PowerShell and from `cmd.exe`, and checks that a tampered download is refused by both the installer and `fgctl init`.
  - **Not covered.** Windows ARM64 and macOS have no asset. The machine release store stays at `%USERPROFILE%\.local\state\fgos` (`FGOS_STATE_HOME` moves it); relocating it to `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is a separate decision.
- **RUL17 (one `fgos` on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos; `doctor --fix` provides it; 2026-10-13).** A release install puts only `fgctl` on PATH and `fgctl init` activates a release per project, so a plain `fgos` used to need an absolute path. `fgos doctor` check `project-fgos-launcher` and its registered fix own the answer, and `fgctl init` already ends by running `doctor --fix`:
  - The fix writes one small launcher named `fgos` (`fgos.cmd` on Windows) into the directory `fgctl` was found in on `PATH`. The launcher walks up from the working directory to the nearest `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos` and runs it with the same arguments, so each project runs the release it activated, from any subdirectory, in any shell, interactive or not; it edits no rc file. Outside a project it exits 127 and says to run `fgctl init`.
  - The launcher carries a marker line. The check reports `ready`, an out-of-date copy (rewritten by the fix), a foreign `fgos` found first on `PATH` (never overwritten; the check names it), no `fgos` with `fgctl` on `PATH` (the fix writes it), or neither on `PATH` (the check says to add the directory `fgctl` was installed into).
  - A source checkout keeps the sourced shell-integration script and needs no launcher; the check passes there.
  - Proof: `test/setup/project-launcher.test.mjs` (two projects and a nested one each run their own fgos; the `cmd` launcher runs on Windows in the focused Windows job).

- **RUL14 (the lazy-probe unlock rule: moved).** The rule that unlocks an account locked for a dead login with one real call now lives with the provider-capacity rules in `docs/specs/runner.md` (RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds)), together with the refresh-ahead and write-back rules for a rotating login (RUL75 (a rotating provider login is renewed once at the source, in a copy fgOS holds, and a login renewed inside a private home is written back)). This document keeps only where the state lives (row 5d).
- **RUL15 (`fgctl init` needs no hand-downloaded tarball: it picks its release by a fixed precedence and downloads it checksum-verified; 2026-10-12).** The release `fgctl init` installs comes from the first of these that is set:
  1. `--from <path | URL>` on the command line;
  2. the `FGCTL_FROM=<path | URL>` environment variable (same meaning as the flag, for a non-release build: a `.tar.gz`, a release directory, or a URL);
  3. `FGCTL_VERSION=<tag>`, which downloads exactly that tag's asset (needed for a pre-release, which "latest" never selects);
  4. the release pinned by the project's committed `.fgos/distribution.json` (no network when that release is staged on the machine; otherwise see "The pin records the tag" below);
  5. otherwise the latest GitHub release, found by following `<repo>/releases/latest` to its tag.
  - An explicit source (1-3) beats a pin; the pin then only validates what was fetched (a different digest is refused as a pin mismatch, as for `--from` today). The inputs are read per invocation; nothing is remembered.
  - **The pin records the tag.** When `fgctl init` installs from a download (latest or `FGCTL_VERSION`) and writes a new `.fgos/distribution.json`, it stores the resolved tag in `projectRuntime.releaseVersion` next to the digest (a local or URL source writes a digest-only pin with a null `releaseVersion`, never the build's own manifest version, which is not a download name; an existing pin is never rewritten). A pin with a tag whose digest is not staged on this machine (a teammate's fresh clone, or a quarantined release) makes a plain `fgctl init` download that tag, checksum-verified; the pin's digest must equal what was fetched, else `pin-mismatch` and nothing is activated. A tag written without the leading `v` (a hand-edited pin, for example `0.2.0`) is read as `v0.2.0`, the form releases are tagged in; if the download still fails, the error names the pinned tag and points to `FGCTL_VERSION` and `FGCTL_FROM` instead of surfacing a bare HTTP error. A digest-only pin (no tag) keeps the old behavior: it needs `--from`, `FGCTL_FROM` or `FGCTL_VERSION` on a machine that has not staged it. `fgctl upgrade` writes no tag (it takes a local path), so an upgraded pin goes back to digest-only unless the manifest carries its own version.

```text
## Lịch sử quyết định

- **2026-10-12 — `fgctl init` downloads by default (RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given)).** Before this, a plain `fgctl init` in a project with no pin failed with "`--from <source>` is required", so a first install meant downloading the release tarball by hand. Owner decision: no source and no pin means the latest GitHub release; `FGCTL_VERSION` selects an exact tag; `FGCTL_FROM` and `--from` select a non-release build; checksum verification is mandatory; the transport is the system `curl` rather than a new HTTP crate (same behavior and override as `install.sh`, no TLS stack to carry in `fgctl`). Prior art: `fgctl init --from` (the release-asset door, kept unchanged and now equivalent to `FGCTL_FROM`), `install.sh`'s `FGCTL_VERSION`/`FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL`/`FGCTL_TARGET` (reused, not redefined). Same day, follow-up: the pin now records the tag, so a pinned workspace whose release is not staged on this machine downloads it instead of needing a source; only a digest-only legacy pin still needs `FGCTL_FROM`/`FGCTL_VERSION`/`--from`, because a digest names no download. Follow-up (2026-10-14): `fgctl upgrade` uses the same verified download pipeline (`--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > latest GitHub release) and records the downloaded tag in `.fgos/distribution.json`, so an upgraded project's pin keeps a downloadable `releaseVersion` for teammates instead of reverting to digest-only.
- **2026-10-13 — Windows is a native release target (RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)).** Owner decision: the level is "native, complete" (PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, no Git Bash, no WSL), with `tar.gz` kept as the single archive format and macOS left out of scope. Prior art, reused: the Windows CI hardening track made the Rust workspace build and the release-tree staging work on Windows (the `fgos.exe` entry, colon-free release store directory names, drive-letter-safe archive validation), and an earlier change wrote `.cmd` launchers on Windows that ran the `sh` shims through a `sh` on `PATH`; that required Git for Windows, so it is replaced by launchers that read `activation.json` themselves. Missing before: a Windows release asset, `install.ps1`, a Windows consumer proof, and any check that the launchers exist. Also in this change: the Linux asset moves from `ubuntu-latest` (binaries then needed glibc 2.39 and printed a loader warning on Ubuntu 22.04, glibc 2.35) to `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate on the glibc symbol versions.
```

Prior art: `fgctl init --from` (the release-asset door, kept unchanged and now equivalent to `FGCTL_FROM`), `install.sh`'s `FGCTL_VERSION`/`FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL`/`FGCTL_TARGET` (reused, not redefined). Same day, follow-up: the pin now records the tag, so a pinned workspace whose release is not staged on this machine downloads it instead of needing a source; only a digest-only legacy pin still needs `FGCTL_FROM`/`FGCTL_VERSION`/`--from`, because a digest names no download.\n- **2026-10-13 — Windows is a native release target (RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)).** Owner decision: the level is \"native, complete\" (PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, no Git Bash, no WSL), with `tar.gz` kept as the single archive format and macOS left out of scope. Prior art, reused: the Windows CI hardening track made the Rust workspace build and the release-tree staging work on Windows (the `fgos.exe` entry, colon-free release store directory names, drive-letter-safe archive validation), and an earlier change wrote `.cmd` launchers on Windows that ran the `sh` shims through a `sh` on `PATH`; that required Git for Windows, so it is replaced by launchers that read `activation.json` themselves. Missing before: a Windows release asset, `install.ps1`, a Windows consumer proof, and any check that the launchers exist. Also in this change: the Linux asset moves from `ubuntu-latest` (binaries then needed glibc 2.39 and printed a loader warning on Ubuntu 22.04, glibc 2.35) to `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate on the glibc symbol versions."
  }
}

Path/anchor: docs/specs/distribution.md#edge-cases-settled
Content commit: b1e53b4fb0e99963328e84b63a4764c0d87abb21
Native digest: 1222a356730459a58d03ca68ada07f9dbd0d21cc6d6dcfba18067b6fddf7902d
Shown text SHA256: 56b4304f887a3915cedec0283794bc200cb764bca44912fc45884a5351dd5583
Lines: 327 to 327

```text
## Edge Cases Settled

- A package marked as not intended for public registry publication can still
  be installed directly from its GitHub repository — that restriction only
  blocks publishing to a public registry, not this installation path.
- Both CLI entry points (`fgos` and `fgos-runner`) are installed identically,
  executable immediately after install — a fresh install does not require
  the installer to separately locate or make executable the autonomous-loop
  runner command.
- Calling `fgos`/`fgos-runner` (via the dev checkout shell helper) from
  inside a linked git worktree of this repository always runs the MAIN
  checkout's entry point, never that worktree's own local copy — accepted
  as-is for this mechanism, not treated as a defect.
- A package manager whose own policy blocks lifecycle scripts for
  git-hosted dependencies (e.g. pnpm 10+'s `allowBuilds`) never blocks
  installing this package, because this package's install never declares a
  lifecycle script in the first place (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle) —
  there is nothing for that policy to approve or refuse.
- `fgos setup` run a second time with nothing new to do reports that
  plainly rather than silently repeating (or silently no-oping without
  saying so).
- `fgos doctor`'s `config-not-stale` check on a machine where `fgos setup`
  was never run reports "not configured yet", not an error and not a
  silently-created file.
- A release tree staged for `fgctl` (`scripts/build-rust-distribution.mjs`)
  carries the legacy-node payload TOGETHER WITH its production dependencies
  (the package's `dependencies` and theirs), copied next to the sources, so
  every verb runs from the installed release alone. Before this, the staged
  tree held no dependencies and any verb that loads one (`fgos workflow`,
  found when dogfooding a project that had run `fgctl init`) failed with a
  missing-package error while `fgos version` and `fgos doctor` still passed.
  A dependency that is not installed when the tree is built fails the build
  instead of thinning the payload; two installed copies of one name are
  refused. The external-consumer CI step runs a dependency-loading verb for
  this reason, because `version` never imports one.
- An agent in a project with no `bin/` (only the installed `fgos`) finds how
  to run anything from `fgos --help --json` and `fgos <verb> [<sub>] --help
  --json`. The host's route table carries two option selectors, `--help` and
  `-h`, generated from `HELP_SELECTORS` in `src/cli/command-registry.mjs`
  like every verb route and sent to the legacy-node payload, which owns the
  verb manifest; every other leading option still has no route and exits 4.
  A Rust-native verb given an exact `--help`/`-h` token anywhere after it is
  sent to the payload too, so it prints its manifest entry instead of
  running. `fgos version` lists verbs only, never the two help selectors.
```

### Complete target / successor

Content commit: b1e53b4fb0e99963328e84b63a4764c0d87abb21

Shown text SHA256: 9d431d903923af6fed1b346a65e0b7d0d0d63b6613b8cc742bd0d6651be8374b
Lines: 711 to 711

```text
#### Edge Cases Settled

- A package marked as not intended for public registry publication can still
  be installed directly from its GitHub repository — that restriction only
  blocks publishing to a public registry, not this installation path.
- Both CLI entry points (`fgos` and `fgos-runner`) are installed identically,
  executable immediately after install — a fresh install does not require
  the installer to separately locate or make executable the autonomous-loop
  runner command.
- Calling `fgos`/`fgos-runner` (via the dev checkout shell helper) from
  inside a linked git worktree of this repository always runs the MAIN
  checkout's entry point, never that worktree's own local copy — accepted
  as-is for this mechanism, not treated as a defect.
- A package manager whose own policy blocks lifecycle scripts for
  git-hosted dependencies (e.g. pnpm 10+'s `allowBuilds`) never blocks
  installing this package, because this package's install never declares a
  lifecycle script in the first place (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle) —
  there is nothing for that policy to approve or refuse.
- `fgos setup` run a second time with nothing new to do reports that
  plainly rather than silently repeating (or silently no-oping without
  saying so).
- `fgos doctor`'s `config-not-stale` check on a machine where `fgos setup`
  was never run reports "not configured yet", not an error and not a
  silently-created file.
- A release tree staged for `fgctl` (`scripts/build-rust-distribution.mjs`)
  carries the legacy-node payload TOGETHER WITH its production dependencies
  (the package's `dependencies` and theirs), copied next to the sources, so
  every verb runs from the installed release alone. Before this, the staged
  tree held no dependencies and any verb that loads one (`fgos workflow`,
  found when dogfooding a project that had run `fgctl init`) failed with a
  missing-package error while `fgos version` and `fgos doctor` still passed.
  A dependency that is not installed when the tree is built fails the build
  instead of thinning the payload; two installed copies of one name are
  refused. The external-consumer CI step runs a dependency-loading verb for
  this reason, because `version` never imports one.
```

```text
- A package marked as not intended for public registry publication can still
  be installed directly from its GitHub repository — that restriction only
  blocks publishing to a public registry, not this installation path.
- Both CLI entry points (`fgos` and `fgos-runner`) are installed identically,
  executable immediately after install — a fresh install does not require
  the installer to separately locate or make executable the autonomous-loop
  runner command.
- Calling `fgos`/`fgos-runner` (via the dev checkout shell helper) from
  inside a linked git worktree of this repository always runs the MAIN
  checkout's entry point, never that worktree's own local copy — accepted
  as-is for this mechanism, not treated as a defect.
- A package manager whose own policy blocks lifecycle scripts for
  git-hosted dependencies (e.g. pnpm 10+'s `allowBuilds`) never blocks
  installing this package, because this package's install never declares a
  lifecycle script in the first place (per str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle) —
  there is nothing for that policy to approve or refuse.
- `fgos setup` run a second time with nothing new to do reports that
  plainly rather than silently repeating (or silently no-oping without
  saying so).
- `fgos doctor`'s `config-not-stale` check on a machine where `fgos setup`
  was never run reports "not configured yet", not an error and not a
  silently-created file.
- A release tree staged for `fgctl` (`scripts/build-rust-distribution.mjs`)
  carries the legacy-node payload TOGETHER WITH its production dependencies
  (the package's `dependencies` and theirs), copied next to the sources, so
  every verb runs from the installed release alone. Before this, the staged
  tree held no dependencies and any verb that loads one (`fgos workflow`,
  found when dogfooding a project that had run `fgctl init`) failed with a
  missing-package error while `fgos version` and `fgos doctor` still passed.
  A dependency that is not installed when the tree is built fails the build
  instead of thinning the payload; two installed copies of one name are
  refused. The external-consumer CI step runs a dependency-loading verb for
  this reason, because `version` never imports one.
```

`catchup` (bin/fgos.mjs) dùng lại cùng cơ chế git cho cả tầng con→gốc lẫn gốc→cây chính; `isMainWorktree` (STR44) — chặn cấu trúc (không dựa sổ đăng ký session) xác nhận `cwd` LÀ worktree chính trước khi `approve` merge/verify, bắt cả worktree tay không đăng ký qua `fgos session start` — cùng `detectTrunk` nay ở `src/runner/worktree.mjs` (theo tsk-49i), không còn ở file này; spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `src/verbs/<domain>/<verb>.mjs` — tầng use-case của CLI (theo tsk-49i): logic nghiệp vụ của một verb, chữ ký thống nhất `<verb>UseCase(ctx, options)` — `ctx` là thứ adapter tính từ môi trường (`{dir, cwd?, repoRoot?}`, use-case KHÔNG BAO GIỜ tự đọc `process.cwd()`/`process.env`/argv), `options` là flag đã parse; trả đúng payload `fgos.v1` (bọc envelope + map exit-code vẫn ở `bin/fgos.mjs`), refusal vẫn `throw StoreError`. Cụm đầu tiên: `src/verbs/merge/` (`merge`/`approve`/`review`/`sync-root`/`catchup`/`reject`/`promote-to-component`) — `bin/fgos.mjs` cho 7 verb này nay chỉ parse args, tính `repoRoot` theo chính sách RIÊNG của từng verb, gọi một hàm use-case. Không ngụ ý migrate 7 file use-case-rank sẵn có (`runner/loop.mjs`, `intake/*`, `setup/*`, `state/cursor.mjs`); spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `src/report/item-trace.mjs` — trace outcome/friction của MỘT item, đọc thuần trên view (`collectOutcomeEntry`/`collectFrictionData`/`collectReviewTrace`); dùng chung bởi `review` (use-case) và `check`/`show`/`doc-sources`/`evolve` (`bin/fgos.mjs`); spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `src/runner/github-adapter.mjs` — vận chuyển GitHub thuần cho cổng duyệt PR nội bộ (`createGitHubPR`/`viewGitHubPRStatus`/`mergeGitHubPR`/`classifyGhFailure`, shell ra `gh` CLI thật, layer infra), dùng bởi `bin/fgos.mjs` verb `review`/`approve --github`; spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `src/runner/worker-log.mjs` — cửa ghi DUY NHẤT cho bản ghi output cục bộ của trợ lý (`.fgos/logs/<id>.log`, git-ignored): `appendWorkerLog` — khối kết-cục cuối, gọi bởi `loop.mjs` sau mỗi lượt dispatch; `appendWorkerLogChunk` — live tee từng chunk stdout/stderr khi đến (STR39), gọi bởi `dispatch.mjs`'s `spawnWorker` qua `opts.onChunk`; spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `src/runner/session.mjs` — vòng đời phiên checkout đa-phiên tùy chọn (fgos-multi-session-checkout, STR35): `createSession`/`endSession`/`listSessions`/`reclaimOrphanedSessions`, worktree detached-HEAD mỗi phiên (`git worktree add --detach`), `.fgos` symlink dùng chung (KHÔNG BAO GIỜ sao chép), sổ `.fgos/sessions.json` canh bởi `.fgos/sessions.lock` riêng; dùng bởi `bin/fgos.mjs` verb `session`; spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `packages/observe/rust/src/metrics_cli/entropy.rs` — tín hiệu entropy-trend + đếm compounding (thuần, đọc trên view work-state), surfaced qua `fgos metrics entropy`; spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `src/report/enduser-index.mjs` — bộ sinh CHỈ MỤC đọc-theo-tag tài liệu người-dùng-cuối (thuần, không I/O — mirror `entropy.mjs`): `QUADRANTS`, bảng nguồn-sự-thật `QUADRANT_META` (quadrant→{purpose,audience}), `QUADRANT_DIR_ALIASES` (quadrant→vị trí thay thế trên đĩa, theo str64-backfill; hiện `explanation`→`['decisions']`), `findSourceCaptureId` (gom một, cho chỉ mục), `findSourceCaptureIds` (gom mọi capture của một đường dẫn, cho `doc-sources`), `buildEnduserIndex`; I/O + verb `fgos docs-index` (quét cả thư mục chính lẫn `QUADRANT_DIR_ALIASES`, ghi manifest `docs/enduser-docs-index.json`) và verb `fgos doc-sources <docPath>` (gom nguồn của một đường dẫn) sống ở `bin/fgos.mjs`, cả hai quyền `read`; vận hành chỉ mục: kỹ năng `fgos-indexing`; spec: docs/specs/enduser-docs-index.md\n- `src/report/frontmatter.mjs` — bộ đọc/ghi đầu-mô-tả OKF-style của mỗi tài liệu người-dùng-cuối (thuần, không I/O, không phụ thuộc thư viện ngoài — theo str64-backfill): `parseFrontmatter`/`renderFrontmatter` (loại/tiêu đề/nhãn/thời điểm/móc-liên-kết-nguồn); tách biệt với bộ sinh chỉ mục — đầu-mô-tả là bản sao ghi-lúc-soạn, KHÔNG phải nguồn thẩm quyền của linkage; spec: docs/specs/enduser-docs-index.md\n- `src/evolve/candidates.mjs` — Gate A candidate ranking cho vòng tự cải thiện (self-improve loop, STR13 Slice 1): thuần, đọc trên view work-state, dùng lại `entropy.mjs`'s `listUnsettledFrictionsByWork`/`WEIGHTS.frictionUnsettled` (không tự định nghĩa lại); surfaced qua `fgos evolve` (liệt kê + `--pick <id>`, hai bước, không stdin); spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `src/state/impact.mjs` — backlog-triage impact ranking (STR21, cửa 2 của triage — tách bạch khỏi STR14 intake-triage): thuần, xếp hạng item CHƯA `done` theo `blocks` (số item khác chưa `done` liệt kê nó trong `deps`); surfaced qua `fgos triage`; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md\n- `src/state/awaiting-context.mjs` — neo gốc cho cổng chờ-người (str61-chat-context-continuity): thuần, đọc trên view work-state, tính `{parent, changedSinceAsk?}` cho một item `awaiting-human` có `parent` mỗi lần đọc (không lưu trữ); surfaced qua `fgos list`'s khóa cộng thêm `awaitingContext`; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §RUL45 (awaitingContext — neo gốc cho cổng chờ-người, dẫn xuất đọc-thời-điểm)\n- `src/intake/risk-keywords.mjs` — nguồn duy nhất của `HEAVY_KEYWORDS` (self-improve loop STR13 Slice 2, kernel layer, dùng chung giữa `classify.mjs` và `iron-law.mjs`); spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `src/evolve/iron-law.mjs` — Iron Law risk classifier cho vòng tự cải thiện (self-improve loop, STR13 Slice 2): thuần, chưa có call site (Slice 3 wiring); spec: docs/specs/runner.md\n- `docs/specs/observe.md` — spec thành phần Observe (đo lường `fgos metrics` và ghi nhận `fgos friction` trọn sang Rust); Rubric: `docs/reference/discussion-quality-rubric.md`; cách so sánh mù: `docs/how-to/compare-discussion-setups-with-metrics-eval.md`.\n- `test/` — node:test suite (`npm test`, 2970 test): smoke + state + cli + runner + report + e2e (rebuild-determinism, runner-loop — gồm kịch bản cửa pull S2-pull + con fork từ tip nhánh gốc, pr-gate — 4 kịch bản trọn vòng review/approve/reject, dispatch song song thật với cửa sổ chồng-lấn đo được); benchmark ngoài suite (F4) tại `docs/history/phase-3-compound-learning/reports/f4-benchmark.md`\n- `scripts/run-test-canary.mjs` (`npm run test:canary -- <file...>`) + `scripts/test-select.mjs` (`npm run test:related -- --explain`, plus `test:related:shadow` for evidence-gathering; manifest: `test/test-ownership.mjs`) — additive fast test-feedback doors, `npm test` unchanged/authoritative either way; how-to: `docs/how-to/use-fast-test-feedback-commands.md`; plan: `plans/260920-immediate-test-feedback-reduction/plan.md`\n- `.fgos/events.jsonl` — nhật ký sự kiện work-state (truth, committed); `.fgos/state.json` là view gitignored; `.fgos/logs/<id>.log` — bản ghi output cục bộ của trợ lý theo từng việc, gitignored (spec: docs/specs/runner.md)\n- `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` — doctrine layer nạp mọi phiên agent (bản sản phẩm — thuần forgent)"

    "sectionText": "# Reading Map (sản phẩm)\n\n> **Quy tắc chuyển tiếp hiện hành:** bắt đầu ở `docs/reading-map.md` và `docs/platform/README.md`\n> (hoặc tra cứu nhanh tại `docs/transitional-switchboard.md`), rồi dùng mapping current-source tường minh của\n> portal area. Không suy authority từ path, ngày review, độ chi tiết, hoặc\n> riêng metadata `Canonical:`. Bảng kiểm chứng Phase 00 sống tại\n> `plans/260925-documentation-authority-unification/current-authority-map-2026-09-25.md`;\n> bảng đó không promote, migrate hay retire source nào. Phase 00 và Phase 01 đã\n> hoàn tất; Phase 02–09 vẫn chưa được authorize.\n\n- `docs/platform-foundations.md` — văn bản gốc 8 luật nền platform (L1–L8); spec: docs/specs/platform-foundations.md\n- `docs/backlog.md` — product backlog (PBI rows, scribing-owned)\n- `docs/architecture-map.md` — bản chuẩn kiến trúc (v0.2, record ADR0010 (bản đồ kiến trúc là bản chuẩn)): 5 tầng + 2 lớp phủ, sổ component + sổ contract (CTR001–CTR009), nghi thức thẻ-căn-cước-trước-code\n- `docs/work-item-lifecycle-vision.md` — tầm nhìn nền tảng: chu trình sống của work-item (mixed-autonomy, base-workflow + domain-extension); khung cho các PBI STR14-STR18\n- `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/README.md` — portal hiện hành cho packaging/distribution: `fgctl` bootstrap/init/repair/upgrade, workspace activation, doctor/fix readiness, legacy Node compatibility, skill/instruction projections. Khi mục này mâu thuẫn với `docs/specs/distribution.md`, đọc portal + implementation-alignment trước; `docs/specs/distribution.md` hiện là legacy/generated-curated source trong lúc migration.\n- `docs/distribution-vision.md` — tầm nhìn nền tảng lịch sử: cài đặt/setup/doctor ổn định + tái dùng được (không cần clone, global/project không xung đột — project ghi đè global, doctor/setup tự fix hạ tầng + merge config thiếu, module mới tự đăng ký năng lực config, CI như một phần của setup); đã được promote/supersede từng phần vào `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/vision.md`.\n- `docs/specs/` — state layer: area spec + system-overview + bản đồ này\n- `docs/routing-handoff-contract.md` — hợp đồng handoff agent↔agent + ranh giới tin cậy\n- `docs/io-contract.md` — hợp đồng giao tiếp VÀO/RA của cửa CLI + bề mặt stdout `fgos-runner` (str46-io-contract): danh tính `writer`/`role`, envelope `fgos.v1` + ngoại lệ có lý do, exit-code một nguồn, sổ verb (`touchesState`/`externalEffect`/`paginated`/`multiValueFormat`), version token, ranh giới ngoài (STR38/STR48/STR83)\n- `docs/coexistence.md` — doctrine chạy cạnh một harness agent khác (record ADR0009 (chống giao thoa lúc cài — fgOS khi cài không giao thoa tiến trình với harness khác)): lãnh địa, một-nhạc-trưởng-mỗi-phiên, nhường-nhịn lúc `init`, manifest `.fgos/coexistence.json`, Known Gaps chưa flip; `src/install/coexist.mjs` — cài đặt detection + manifest (read-only, không đè)\n- `package.json` (`version`, `files`, `bin.fgos`, `bin.fgos-runner`) + `README.md` (mục `## Install`) — cài `fgos` VÀ `fgos-runner` từ ngoài source repo qua GitHub install, cả hai executable ngay sau cài; `test/install-packaging.test.mjs` — proof e2e (pack → install → chạy từ project ngoài, gồm cả hai binary); spec: docs/specs/distribution.md\n- `scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh` — dev checkout shell helper (STR87 first slice): hàm `fgos`/`fgos-runner` tự resolve root qua `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (worktree-safe), source từ shell profile của contributor, không cài đặt gì; test: `test/scripts/fgos-shell-integration.test.mjs`; spec: docs/specs/distribution.md §Dev checkout shell helpers\n- `src/setup/` (`ansi.mjs`, `config-merge.mjs`, `shell-rc.mjs`, `checks.mjs`) + `bin/fgos.mjs`'s current legacy `setup`/`doctor` verbs + `src/cli/command-registry.mjs` entries — doctor/fix registry and legacy setup compatibility: `doctor` chẩn đoán read-only, `doctor --fix` chạy registered fixes, current Node `fgos setup` vẫn tồn tại nhưng target architecture supersedes onboarding bằng `fgctl init` + local `fgos init` / `fgos doctor --fix` / `fgos doctor`; manifest: `docs/architecture-manifest.json`; test: `test/setup/*.test.mjs`; current portal: `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/README.md`; legacy spec: docs/specs/distribution.md §Setup, §Doctor\n- `docs/decisions/` — hồ sơ quyết định dài hạn cho người ngoài (decision records); từ str64-backfill, mỗi record còn mang đầu-mô-tả OKF-style (loại/tiêu đề/nhãn/thời điểm/móc-liên-kết-nguồn, xem `frontmatter.mjs` dòng dưới) và được `fgos docs-index` công nhận là vị trí thay thế của ngăn `explanation` (R10, spec: docs/specs/enduser-docs-index.md) — thân ADR không đổi, chỉ thêm đầu-mô-tả; lưu ý `orchestrator` là pinned term đã đổi nghĩa giữa chừng (0026→0028 nghĩa cũ \"launcher\", 0029 nghĩa mới \"tầng hợp thành T0\"; xem chuỗi quyết định tại `docs/decisions/index.md` dòng 28-32)\n- `scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.mjs` + `test/scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.test.mjs` — quét `docs/backlog.md` + `docs/specs/*.md` tìm dòng còn trích một quyết định đã bị supersede mà không nhắc quyết định thay thế trên cùng dòng (STR72 CoS clause 2, PBI p-2d71dfc3); chỉ phát hiện, không tự sửa; spec: docs/specs/decision-citation-drift.md\n- `scripts/check-decision-codes.mjs` + `test/scripts/check-decision-codes.test.mjs` — quét `test/**/*.test.mjs` tìm tên test còn nhúng mã quyết định nội bộ (str##/D#/RUL##/STR##/tsk-xxx) thay vì mô tả bất biến bằng lời thường (review-audit-self-decision.md mục Stable Code Artifacts); chặn (ratchet) chỉ vi phạm MỚI so với `scripts/check-decision-codes.baseline.json` đã chốt, không chặn ngược nợ cũ; `npm test` tự chạy qua glob `test/**/*.test.mjs`, không hook riêng\n- `docs/id-systems-audit.md` — audit + quyết định hình dạng mọi hệ id/mã đang sống trong hệ thống (work.id/kind/Story/ADR/Rule/Contract phía fgOS; D-hex/D-local/cell-id/feature-slug/severity phía bee) — nguồn cho `work.id`'s `tsk-<hash>` và các migration STR53-STR58 (tất cả đã `done`); boundary appendix: `docs/architecture-map.md` Phụ lục B\n- `bin/fgos.mjs` — CLI một cửa của work-state; chạy `node bin/fgos.mjs <verb>`; gồm verb `edit` — sửa đè các trường (title/kind/risk/verify/tier/refs/deps/acceptance/priority/intent — str7-str8-priority-intent) trên một item đã có, cùng cửa ghi CTR002 như `add`/`move`; gồm verb `take`/`return` — cửa pull giao–nhận việc cho tác nhân ngoài runner; gồm verb `pick` — cửa pull GỘP `take` + dựng workspace (`createWorktree`), role cố định `session`, không cờ `--role` (theo str83-fgos-slash-commands); gồm verb `review`/`approve`/`reject` — cổng duyệt PR nội bộ, một cổng cho mọi đề xuất `awaiting-approval`, nay leaf-vs-root-aware (con nhập vào nhánh của gốc, gốc nhập vào cây chính); `review`/`approve` nay chấp nhận thêm `--github [--pr <n>]` — vận chuyển thay thế CÙNG cổng duyệt qua GitHub thay vì diff/merge cục bộ (chỉ nguồn runner, theo github-adapter, spec: docs/specs/runner.md); gồm verb `catchup` — đồng bộ lại một việc đỗ vì gãy nhập/trôi tích hợp (spec: docs/specs/runner.md); gồm verb `session` (`start`/`end`/`list`) — vòng đời phiên checkout đa-phiên tùy chọn, mỗi phiên một worktree detached-HEAD cho cây nguồn, dùng chung MỘT kho `.fgos/` qua symlink (spec: docs/specs/runner.md); spec: docs/specs/work-state.md\n- `src/state/` — lõi work-state: events (nhật ký; `appendEvent` nay khóa liên-tiến-trình `.fgos/events.lock`, per fgos-multi-session-checkout Epic 3/STR35 — xem spec Work-State RUL10 (tiền đề có ngưỡng — một người ghi tại một thời điểm; multi-agent ghi đồng thời qua `.fgos/events.lock`)), work (schema — STATUSES + STAGES + field `parent` lineage + field `domain`), fsm (bảng chuyển status + CAS), stage (bảng chuyển stage + CAS, chiều vĩ mô song song fsm; cạnh chuyển-stage tra theo domain của item — `coding`: `discovery → exploring → planning → executing`, trong đó phán-quyết `clear` ở `discovery` bỏ qua `exploring` để sang thẳng `planning` còn `unclear` đi qua `exploring`; tên `decompose` vẫn còn nhưng chỉ là bí danh legacy chỉ-để-rút-cạn (không việc MỚI nào vào được nữa); `synthetic`: một stage, không cạnh nào), domains (sổ đăng ký domain — stage list + step-mapping base-workflow + cạnh-chuyển mỗi domain; `coding` + ba domain minh họa/thử-nghiệm `synthetic` (đúng một stage), `triage`, `fixture-marketing`; base-workflow-model STR18, hoàn tất S1+S2), replay (fold), frontier (truy vấn sẵn-sàng — lọc theo status, stage domain-aware, VÀ lineage qua `parent`), dep-graph (dò chu trình trên `deps` — bất biến phi-chu-trình tại cửa ghi, per work-graph-intelligence S1), store (chủ ghi duy nhất + readRawEvents), envelope (phong bì output CTR001, `wrapEnvelope` — nay bọc MỌI verb ở một cửa in trong `bin/fgos.mjs main()`, STR37; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §envelope)\n- `src/cli/command-registry.mjs` — sổ verb máy-đọc của CLI (STR37, kernel, thuần dữ liệu): `SCHEMA_VERSION` + `COMMAND_REGISTRY` (mọi verb với `{name, invoke, description, parameters, examples, access read|mutation, deprecated}`); `bin/fgos.mjs` `--help [--json]` và `<verb> [<sub>] --help [--json]` sinh sổ từ đây; verb có sub-verb mang `subcommands`, `HELP_SELECTORS` (`--help`, `-h`) thành route của Rust host qua `scripts/export-command-selectors.mjs`;
